Hello @yonghao2011, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request primarily introduces robust proxy support to the ccusage tool, enabling it to function correctly in network-restricted environments by automatically detecting and utilizing proxy settings for fetching essential pricing data. This resolves issues where users in certain regions could not fetch data without workarounds. Additionally, it includes a substantial cleanup and simplification of the project's package.json file.
Highlights

Network Proxy Support: Implemented automatic proxy detection using http_proxy, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, and HTTPS_PROXY environment variables to enable ccusage to fetch pricing data in network-restricted environments.
Undici ProxyAgent Integration: Integrated undici's ProxyAgent for all fetch requests that require proxying, ensuring proper routing of network traffic for external data retrieval.
Build-Time Proxy Support: Extended proxy functionality to the build process, specifically for pre-fetching Claude pricing data via src/_macro.ts, resolving potential build failures in restricted networks.
Debugging & Observability: Added informative logging to src/pricing-fetcher.ts to indicate when a proxy is detected and being used, aiding in troubleshooting network connectivity issues.
Project Configuration Cleanup: Performed a significant cleanup and reduction of the package.json file, removing various development-related scripts, dependencies, and configurations, streamlining the project setup.

node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR adds automatic proxy support to resolve network connectivity issues in environments with restricted access to GitHub (such as mainland China).
Changes Made

Automatic proxy detection: Checks for http_proxy, https_proxy, HTTP_PROXY, and HTTPS_PROXY environment variables
Undici ProxyAgent integration: Uses undici's ProxyAgent for fetch requests when proxy is configured
Build-time support: Extends proxy support to macro execution during build process
Debug logging: Adds informative logging when proxy is detected and used

Files Modified

src/pricing-fetcher.ts: Added proxy detection and ProxyAgent usage in ensurePricingLoaded()
src/_macro.ts: Added proxy support for build-time pricing data fetching

Problem Solved
Fixes the issue where npx ccusage@latest fails in network-restricted environments due to inability to fetch pricing data from GitHub raw content. Users previously had to use --offline mode or clone the repository locally to work around this limitation.
Testing
Tested successfully with:

Local development environment with proxy
Published test package ccusage-test@15.1.0 via npx with proxy configuration
Verified proxy detection and usage logging

Usage
No changes required for existing users. The tool will automatically detect and use proxy settings from environment variables when available.
Example:
export https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:8888
npx ccusage@latest daily  # Now works in restricted environments
🤖 Generated with Claude Code
Co-Authored-By: Claude noreply@anthropic.com

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added support for routing pricing data fetch requests through a proxy if proxy environment variables are configured.



Chores

Improved logging to indicate when a proxy is being used for fetch operations.

bodyText:
Summary of Changes
Hello @DonDawsy, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request aims to significantly improve the user experience in terminal applications like Warp and iTerm by eliminating screen flicker during display updates. It achieves this by refining the underlying terminal clearing logic, introducing a mechanism to clear only the previously rendered content, and adding small delays to ensure terminal commands are processed smoothly.
Highlights

Enhanced Terminal Clearing: The TerminalManager now leverages node:readline for more precise screen clearing (cursorTo, clearScreenDown) and introduces a new clearPreviousContent method. This new method clears only the previously rendered output by moving the cursor up and clearing lines, which significantly reduces visual flicker during updates.
Improved Write Operations: The write method in TerminalManager has been updated to track the number of lines written (lastContentLines). This line count is crucial for the new clearPreviousContent functionality. Additionally, a new writeRaw method was introduced for writing text without affecting the line tracking, useful for control characters or non-content output.
Flicker Mitigation in Live Monitoring: Small, asynchronous delays (10ms) have been strategically added after terminal.clearScreen() calls within the startLiveMonitoring function. This provides terminal emulators (like Warp and iTerm) sufficient time to process the clear command before new content is written, directly addressing the reported flicker issue. A redundant clearScreen call was also removed from renderLiveDisplay.

node_title: Add --24hour flag to switch between 12-hour and 24-hour time formats
node_bodyText:
📝 Usage Examples
Default 12-hour format:
ccusage blocks
Output: Block Started: 1/15/2024, 2:30:45 PM (2h 15m ago)
24-hour format:
ccusage blocks --24hour
Output: Block Started: 1/15/2024, 14:30:45 (2h 15m ago)
Live monitoring:
ccusage blocks --live --24hour
Shows times like "Started: 14:30:45" instead of "Started: 02:30:45 PM"
Technical Details
Backwards Compatibility
✅ Flag is optional and defaults to 12-hour format
✅ All existing commands work unchanged
✅ Compatible with other flags like --json, --live, --breakdown
Implementation Approach

Summary by CodeRabbit

Added support for displaying times in 12-hour (AM/PM) format via a new command-line option.
Users can now choose between 24-hour and 12-hour time formats for time displays in commands and live monitoring.

New Feature: 24-hour Time Flag: Introduced a new --24hour boolean flag that allows users to switch between the default 12-hour (AM/PM) and 24-hour time formats for all time displays in the application's output.
Date/Time Formatting Utilities: Added two new utility functions, formatDateTime and formatTime, in src/_utils.ts. These functions centralize and standardize date and time formatting, supporting both 12-hour and 24-hour formats, and offer options for including dates, seconds, and compact displays.
Integrated Time Display: The new time formatting logic and the --24hour flag have been integrated into the blocks command. This ensures that time information in both the static block summary table and the live monitoring view dynamically adjusts based on the user's preferred time format.
Backwards Compatibility: The --24hour flag is optional and defaults to false, meaning the application will continue to display times in the 12-hour format by default. This ensures that existing commands and user experiences remain unchanged.

node_title: fix: reduce screen flickering in live monitoring using alternate screen buffer
node_bodyText:
Summary

Implement alternate screen buffer for live monitoring display to eliminate screen flickering
Remove redundant screen clearing operations in the render loop
Add proper cleanup to restore terminal state on exit

Problem
The current implementation clears the entire screen on every refresh cycle, which causes visible flickering on slower terminals or when refresh rates are high. This creates a poor user experience, especially during extended monitoring sessions.
Solution
This PR introduces alternate screen buffer support (similar to how `vim` or `less` work):

Uses ANSI escape sequences to switch to an alternate screen buffer when monitoring starts
The alternate buffer handles screen updates more efficiently, reducing flicker
Automatically restores the original terminal content when monitoring ends

Changes


TerminalManager enhancements:

Added `enterAlternateScreen()` method to switch to alternate buffer
Added `exitAlternateScreen()` method to restore original screen
Updated `cleanup()` to properly exit alternate screen



Live monitoring improvements:

Enter alternate screen when starting live monitoring
Removed redundant `clearScreen()` call before each render
The alternate buffer handles clearing automatically



Test Plan

 Tested live monitoring with `bun run start blocks --active`
 Verified no flickering on terminal refresh
 Confirmed terminal properly restores on exit (Ctrl+C)
 Ensured all tests pass (`bun run test`)
 Code formatting and linting pass (`bun run format` and ESLint)
 TypeScript checks pass (`bun typecheck`)

Impact
This change significantly improves the user experience for live monitoring features without affecting any other functionality. The alternate screen buffer is a standard terminal feature supported by all modern terminal emulators.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Introduced support for alternate screen buffer mode in the terminal, enhancing the live display experience with reduced flicker and improved screen management.



Improvements

Terminal now automatically exits alternate screen buffer mode during cleanup, ensuring a smoother return to the original terminal state after live monitoring sessions.

node_title: Improve `blocks --live` rendering
node_bodyText:
I noticed when I wasn't focused on the terminal in Ghostty, the live terminal had some bad flickering. The cursor was also still being shown.

This addresses that by using the alternate screen provided by terminal emulators.
Also collects all writes and flushes them in a single operation.
Enables DEC mode 2026 for atomic screen updates.
It also makes sure the cursor is hidden.
It also caps the refresh rate at 60fps to preserve CPU

NOTE: only tested in Ghostty
NOTE: couldn't figure out how to auto-format, eslint wasn't doing it, so I used prettier which may have caused too many changes

213-239: Refactor duplicated rendering logic between usage and projections sections.
Both sections follow nearly identical patterns for progress bar creation and detail row formatting. Consider extracting helper functions to reduce duplication and improve maintainability.
Example refactoring approach:
+function renderProgressSection(
+  terminal: TerminalManager,
+  config: { 
+    label: string,
+    icon: string,
+    value: number,
+    limit?: number,
+    barWidth: number,
+    details: Array<{ label: string, value: string }>,
+    marginStr: string,
+    boxWidth: number,
+    labelWidth: number
+  }
+) {
+  const percent = config.limit ? (config.value / config.limit) * 100 : 0;
+  const barColor = percent > 100 ? pc.red : percent > 80 ? pc.yellow : pc.green;
+  
+  const progressBar = config.limit
+    ? createProgressBar(config.value, config.limit, config.barWidth, {
+        showPercentage: false,
+        fillChar: barColor('█'),
+        emptyChar: pc.gray('░'),
+        leftBracket: '[',
+        rightBracket: ']',
+      })
+    : `[${pc.green('█'.repeat(Math.floor(config.barWidth * 0.1)))}${pc.gray('░'.repeat(config.barWidth - Math.floor(config.barWidth * 0.1)))}]`;
+
+  // Render progress bar
+  const labelStr = pc.bold(`${config.icon} ${config.label}`);
+  const labelWidth = stringWidth(labelStr);
+  const suffix = config.limit 
+    ? `${percent.toFixed(1).padStart(6)}% (${formatTokensShort(config.value)}/${formatTokensShort(config.limit)})`
+    : `(${formatTokensShort(config.value)} tokens)`;
+  
+  const barStr = `${labelStr}${''.padEnd(Math.max(0, config.labelWidth - labelWidth))} ${progressBar} ${suffix}`;
+  const barPadded = barStr + ' '.repeat(Math.max(0, config.boxWidth - 3 - stringWidth(barStr)));
+  terminal.write(`${config.marginStr}│ ${barPadded}│\n`);
+
+  // Render details
+  renderDetailRow(terminal, config.details, config.marginStr, config.boxWidth);
+}

-// Usage section rendering (lines 213-239)
+renderProgressSection(terminal, {
+  label: 'USAGE',
+  icon: '🔥',
+  value: totalTokens,
+  limit: config.tokenLimit,
+  barWidth,
+  details: [
+    { label: 'Tokens', value: `${formatNumber(totalTokens)} (${rateDisplay})` },
+    ...(config.tokenLimit ? [{ label: 'Limit', value: `${formatNumber(config.tokenLimit)} tokens` }] : []),
+    { label: 'Cost', value: formatCurrency(block.costUSD) }
+  ],
+  marginStr,
+  boxWidth,
+  labelWidth
+});

node_title: fix: change OGP image from SVG to PNG for better social media compatibility
node_bodyText:
Summary

Changed OGP image format from SVG to PNG in VitePress config
This ensures the logo displays correctly on social media platforms

Problem
Many social platforms (Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn) do not support SVG format for Open Graph Protocol previews, causing the logo to not display properly when sharing links.
Solution
Updated the og:image meta tag to use logo.png instead of logo.svg. The PNG format is universally supported by all major social media platforms.
Test plan

 Deploy changes to production
 Test URL preview on Twitter Card Validator
 Test URL preview on Facebook Sharing Debugger
 Test URL preview on LinkedIn Post Inspector
 Verify logo displays correctly in all platforms

ccusage daily --instances

Multi-Instance Support: Introduces the ability to track Claude Code usage across multiple parallel sessions, enabling monitoring of usage data for each coding project separately.
Project Grouping and Filtering: Adds --instances flag to display usage breakdown by project and --project flag to filter results to specific projects.
Smart Aliases: Allows configuring custom project names via the CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES environment variable.
Enhanced JSON Output: Modifies JSON output to include project-grouped data structure for programmatic consumption.
Improved Path Parsing: Enhances project name extraction from complex directory structures.


Using Gemini Code Assist

The full guide for Gemini Code Assist can be found on our documentation page, here are some quick tips.
Invoking Gemini
You can request assistance from Gemini at any point in your pull request via creating an issue comment (i.e. comment on the pull request page) using either /gemini <command> or @gemini-code-assist <command>. Below is a summary of the supported commands.

Code Review

Responds in comments when explicitly tagged, both in issue comments and review comments.

Customization
To customize Gemini Code Assist for GitHub experience, repository maintainers can create a configuration file and/or provide a custom code review style guide (such as PEP-8 for Python) by creating and adding files to a .gemini/ folder in the base of the repository. Gemini Code Assist is currently in preview and may make mistakes. Please leave feedback on any instances where its feedback is incorrect or counter productive. You can react with 👍 and 👎 on @gemini-code-assist comments to provide feedback.
You can also get AI-powered code generation, chat, as well as code reviews directly in the IDE at no cost with the Gemini Code Assist IDE Extension.

node_title: feat: add project filtering and grouping to daily command
node_bodyText:
Summary
Adds project filtering and grouping support to the daily command for tracking Claude Code usage across multiple parallel sessions.
• Project grouping: New --instances flag displays daily usage breakdown by project
• Project filtering: New --project flag filters daily results to specific projects
• Smart aliases: Configure custom project names via CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES env var
• Enhanced JSON output: Project-grouped data structure for daily reports
• Improved path parsing: Better extraction of meaningful project names from directory structures
Implementation focuses specifically on the daily command with comprehensive project name handling.
Implementation Details

New _project-names.ts module with intelligent project name parsing and alias support
Enhanced daily data loader with project-aware filtering and grouping
Extended daily command interface with --instances and --project flags
Comprehensive test coverage for project name formatting edge cases
Backward compatible - existing daily command usage patterns unchanged

Usage Examples
# Show daily usage by project
ccusage daily --instances

# Filter daily report to specific project 
ccusage daily --project ccusage

# Custom project aliases for daily reports
export CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES="long-project-name=Short Name"
ccusage daily --instances --json
Closes #137
🤖 Generated with Claude Code

Added the ability to group and filter usage data by project using new command-line options (--instances, --project) in daily reports.
Introduced support for custom project name aliases via the CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES environment variable for clearer reporting.
Enhanced JSON and table outputs to display usage breakdowns per project, with improved formatting for project names.



Documentation

Updated user guides and CLI documentation to explain project grouping, filtering, aliasing, and new output formats.
Added detailed examples and usage scenarios for project-level reporting and JSON analysis.



Style

Minor formatting and comment improvements in code for clarity.

node_title: feat: add project filtering and grouping to daily command
node_bodyText:
Summary
Adds project filtering and grouping support to the daily command for tracking Claude Code usage across multiple parallel sessions.
• Project grouping: New --instances flag displays daily usage breakdown by project
• Project filtering: New --project flag filters daily results to specific projects
• Smart aliases: Configure custom project names via CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES env var
• Enhanced JSON output: Project-grouped data structure for daily reports
• Improved path parsing: Better extraction of meaningful project names from directory structures
Implementation focuses specifically on the daily command with comprehensive project name handling.
Implementation Details

New _project-names.ts module with intelligent project name parsing and alias support
Enhanced daily data loader with project-aware filtering and grouping
Extended daily command interface with --instances and --project flags
Comprehensive test coverage for project name formatting edge cases
Backward compatible - existing daily command usage patterns unchanged

Usage Examples
# Show daily usage by project
ccusage daily --instances

# Filter daily report to specific project 
ccusage daily --project ccusage

# Custom project aliases for daily reports
export CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES="long-project-name=Short Name"
ccusage daily --instances --json
Closes #137
🤖 Generated with Claude Code

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added the ability to group and filter usage data by project using new command-line options (--instances, --project) in daily reports.
Introduced support for custom project name aliases via the CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES environment variable for clearer reporting.
Enhanced JSON and table outputs to display usage breakdowns per project, with improved formatting for project names.



Documentation

Updated user guides and CLI documentation to explain project grouping, filtering, aliasing, and new output formats.
Added detailed examples and usage scenarios for project-level reporting and JSON analysis.



Style

Minor formatting and comment improvements in code for clarity.

node_bodyText:
Summary
Adds project filtering and grouping support to the daily command for tracking Claude Code usage across multiple parallel sessions.
• Project grouping: New --instances flag displays daily usage breakdown by project
• Project filtering: New --project flag filters daily results to specific projects
• Smart aliases: Configure custom project names via CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES env var
• Enhanced JSON output: Project-grouped data structure for daily reports
• Improved path parsing: Better extraction of meaningful project names from directory structures
Implementation focuses specifically on the daily command with comprehensive project name handling.
Implementation Details

New _project-names.ts module with intelligent project name parsing and alias support
Enhanced daily data loader with project-aware filtering and grouping
Extended daily command interface with --instances and --project flags
Comprehensive test coverage for project name formatting edge cases
Backward compatible - existing daily command usage patterns unchanged

Usage Examples
# Show daily usage by project
ccusage daily --instances

# Filter daily report to specific project 
ccusage daily --project ccusage

# Custom project aliases for daily reports
export CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES="long-project-name=Short Name"
ccusage daily --instances --json
Closes #137
🤖 Generated with Claude Code

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added the ability to group and filter usage data by project using new command-line options (--instances, --project) in daily reports.
Introduced support for custom project name aliases via the CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES environment variable for clearer reporting.
Enhanced JSON and table outputs to display usage breakdowns per project, with improved formatting for project names.



Documentation

Updated user guides and CLI documentation to explain project grouping, filtering, aliasing, and new output formats.
Added detailed examples and usage scenarios for project-level reporting and JSON analysis.



Style

Minor formatting and comment improvements in code for clarity.

 }
Using path.normalize() is more robust than regex replacement, and trimming the final result ensures clean project names.

 	// Filter by date range if specified

node_title: feat: add project filtering and grouping to daily command
node_bodyText:
Summary
Adds project filtering and grouping support to the daily command for tracking Claude Code usage across multiple parallel sessions.
• Project grouping: New --instances flag displays daily usage breakdown by project
• Project filtering: New --project flag filters daily results to specific projects
• Smart aliases: Configure custom project names via CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES env var
• Enhanced JSON output: Project-grouped data structure for daily reports
• Improved path parsing: Better extraction of meaningful project names from directory structures
Implementation focuses specifically on the daily command with comprehensive project name handling.
Implementation Details

New _project-names.ts module with intelligent project name parsing and alias support
Enhanced daily data loader with project-aware filtering and grouping
Extended daily command interface with --instances and --project flags
Comprehensive test coverage for project name formatting edge cases
Backward compatible - existing daily command usage patterns unchanged

Usage Examples
# Show daily usage by project
ccusage daily --instances

# Filter daily report to specific project 
ccusage daily --project ccusage

# Custom project aliases for daily reports
export CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES="long-project-name=Short Name"
ccusage daily --instances --json
Closes #137
🤖 Generated with Claude Code

New Features

Added the ability to group and filter usage data by project using new command-line options (--instances, --project) in daily reports.
Introduced support for custom project name aliases via the CCUSAGE_PROJECT_ALIASES environment variable for clearer reporting.
Enhanced JSON and table outputs to display usage breakdowns per project, with improved formatting for project names.



Documentation

Updated user guides and CLI documentation to explain project grouping, filtering, aliasing, and new output formats.
Added detailed examples and usage scenarios for project-level reporting and JSON analysis.



Style

Minor formatting and comment improvements in code for clarity.

node_title: feat: add currency conversion support with --currency option
node_bodyText:
Hi! I really love ccusage's minimalist design philosophy, so I'm a bit hesitant to propose this
feature addition.
My personal use case: I wanted to quickly see my Claude costs in JPY without leaving the terminal or
doing manual conversion. So I implemented currency conversion as an optional feature.
Design considerations:

Non-breaking: Defaults to USD, existing behavior unchanged
Opt-in only: Requires explicit --currency  flag
Self-contained: New functionality in separate modules
Daily rate limits: Uses free exchange rate API (open.er-api.com) with 1 request/day limit, cached
locally

Example usage:
ccusage daily --currency JPY  # ¥4,881 instead of $33.35
ccusage monthly --currency EUR # €1,520 instead of $1,755
Implementation scope: This adds comprehensive currency support (25+ currencies with proper
formatting) through two new modules for exchange rate fetching and currency conversion, plus minimal
changes to existing commands to integrate the --currency option.
I understand if this feels too heavy for your core mission.

Hello @kurogedelic, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request significantly enhances the utility of the ccusage tool by adding robust currency conversion capabilities. Users can now specify a target currency to view their AI costs, which are then dynamically converted from USD using real-time exchange rates fetched from an external API and intelligently cached. The implementation is designed to be non-breaking, opt-in, and modular, ensuring maintainability and a smooth user experience.
Highlights

New Feature: Currency Conversion: Introduced a new --currency (or -c) command-line option, allowing users to display Claude AI costs in various international currencies (e.g., JPY, EUR, GBP) instead of the default USD.
Comprehensive Currency Formatting: Enhanced the formatCurrency utility to support over 25 currencies, correctly applying their respective symbols, decimal places, and symbol positioning (before or after the amount).
External API Integration with Caching: Integrated with open.er-api.com to fetch real-time exchange rates. A daily caching mechanism is implemented to store rates locally (~/.claude/ccusage-cache/exchange-rates.json), respecting the API's free tier rate limits (1 request per day).

v20.19.0: 2025-03-13, Version 20.19.0 'Iron' (LTS), @​marco-ippolito
Compare Source
Notable Changes
require(esm) is now enabled by default
Support for loading native ES modules using require() had been available on v20.x under the command line flag --experimental-require-module, and available by default on v22.x and v23.x. In this release, it is now no longer behind a flag on v20.x.
This feature has been tested on v23.x and v22.x, and we are looking for user feedback from v20.x to make more final tweaks before fully stabilizing it. When the Node.js instance encounters a native ES module in require() somewhere outside node_modules for the first time, it will emit an experimental warning unless require() comes from a path that contains node_modules.  If there happens to be any regressions caused by this feature, users can report it to the Node.js issue tracker. Meanwhile this feature can also be disabled using --no-experimental-require-module as a workaround.
With this feature enabled, Node.js will no longer throw ERR_REQUIRE_ESM if require() is used to load a ES module. It can, however, throw ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE if the ES module being loaded or its dependencies contain top-level await. When the ES module is loaded successfully by require(), the returned object will either be a ES module namespace object similar to what's returned by import(), or what gets exported as "module.exports" in the ES module.
Users can check process.features.require_module to see whether require(esm) is enabled in the current Node.js instance. For packages, the "module-sync" exports condition can be used as a way to detect require(esm) support in the current Node.js instance and allow both require() and import to load the same native ES module. See the documentation for more details about this feature.
Contributed by Joyee Cheung in #​55085
Module syntax detection is now enabled by default
Module syntax detection (the --experimental-detect-module flag) is now
enabled by default. Use --no-experimental-detect-module to disable it if
needed.
Syntax detection attempts to run ambiguous files as CommonJS, and if the module
fails to parse as CommonJS due to ES module syntax, Node.js tries again and runs
the file as an ES module.
Ambiguous files are those with a .js or no extension, where the nearest parent
package.json has no "type" field (either "type": "module" or
"type": "commonjs").
Syntax detection should have no performance impact on CommonJS modules, but it
incurs a slight performance penalty for ES modules; add "type": "module" to
the nearest parent package.json file to eliminate the performance cost.
A use case unlocked by this feature is the ability to use ES module syntax in
extensionless scripts with no nearby package.json.
Thanks to Geoffrey Booth for making this work on #​53619.

Notable Changes
⚠️ Deprecations
Instantiating node:http classes without new
Constructing classes like IncomingMessage or ServerResponse without the new
keyword is now discouraged. This clarifies API expectations and aligns with standard
JavaScript behavior. It may warn or error in future versions.
Contributed by Yagiz Nizipli in #​58518.
options.shell = "" in node:child_process
Using an empty string for shell previously had undefined behavior. This change
encourages explicit choices (e.g., shell: true or a shell path) and avoids
relying on implementation quirks.
Contributed by Antoine du Hamel and Renegade334 #​58564.
HTTP/2 priority signaling
The HTTP/2 prioritization API (e.g., stream.priority) is now deprecated due to
poor real-world support. Applications should avoid using priority hints and expect future removal.
Contributed by Matteo Collina and Antoine du Hamel #​58313.
✅ Features graduated to stable
assert.partialDeepStrictEqual()
This method compares only a subset of properties in deep object comparisons,
useful for flexible test assertions. Its stabilization means it's now safe for
general use and won't change unexpectedly in future releases.
Contributed by Ruben Bridgewater in #​57370.

Semver-minor features
🔧 fs.FileHandle.readableWebStream gets autoClose option
This gives developers explicit control over whether the file descriptor should
be closed when the stream ends. Helps avoid subtle resource leaks.
Contributed by James M Snell in #​58548.
🔧 fs.Dir now supports explicit resource management
This improves ergonomics around async iteration of directories. Developers can
now manually control when a directory is closed using .close() or with Symbol.asyncDispose.
Contributed by Antoine du Hamel in #​58206.
📊 http2 gains diagnostics channel: http2.server.stream.finish
Adds observability support for when a stream finishes. Useful for logging,
monitoring, and debugging HTTP/2 behavior without patching internals.
Contributed by Darshan Sen in #​58560.
🔐 Permissions: implicit allow-fs-read to entrypoint
Node.js permissions model now allows read access to the entry file by default.
It makes running permission-restricted apps smoother while preserving security.
Contributed by Rafael Gonzaga in #​58579.
🎨 util.styleText() adds 'none' style
This lets developers remove styling cleanly without hacks. Useful for overriding
inherited terminal styles when composing styled strings.
Contributed by James M Snell in #​58437.

bodyText:
Summary of Changes
Hello @salala01, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request introduces comprehensive support for tracking and displaying Claude API usage limit reset times. It enhances the application's ability to detect usage limit errors, extract the specific reset timestamp from API responses, and then present this crucial information to the user both in the live monitoring interface and through the blocks command's JSON output. This helps users understand when they can resume API calls after hitting a limit.
Highlights

Tracking Claude API Usage Limits: Implemented logic to parse specific Claude API error messages to extract and track the usage limit reset time. This involves enhancing the usageDataSchema to capture relevant error message details and introducing a new utility function getUsageLimitResetTime to extract the timestamp.
Live Monitoring Display: Added a visual warning to the live monitoring display. When a Claude API usage limit is encountered and a future reset time is available, a prominent red message '❌ USAGE LIMIT. RESET AT ' is now displayed, providing immediate feedback to the user.
Data Model and Output Enhancement: Extended the internal data models (LoadedUsageEntry, SessionBlock) to include the usageLimitResetTime. This information is now propagated through the data processing pipeline and is also included in the JSON output of the blocks command, allowing programmatic access to usage limit details.

Summary of Changes
Hello @ryoppippi, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request introduces a significant shift in our error handling strategy by adopting a functional approach using the @praha/byethrow library's Result type. The change aims to enhance code clarity, type safety, and composability by replacing imperative try-catch blocks with explicit success/failure representations. All existing tests continue to pass, ensuring no behavioral regressions.
Highlights

Dependency Addition: I've added the @praha/byethrow library, along with its MCP counterpart, to the project dependencies (package.json, bun.lock, and .mcp.json). This library provides a Result type for functional error handling.
Error Handling Refactor: I've refactored traditional try-catch blocks across 11 locations in 5 files (src/debug.ts, src/data-loader.ts, src/pricing-fetcher.ts, src/_live-monitor.ts, src/commands/_blocks.live.ts) to utilize the new Result.try() pattern. This includes error handling for JSON parsing, file reading, and network operations.
Code Readability and Type Safety: The refactor leverages Result.isFailure() for clearer error checking and improves type safety by explicitly representing success and failure states, aligning with functional programming principles.
Documentation Update: I've updated CLAUDE.md to include new guidelines for error handling, recommending the @praha/byethrow Result type over traditional try-catch for most scenarios.

Hello @Karibash, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request significantly refactors the error handling strategy within the PricingFetcher class and its related components. By adopting a functional approach with the byethrow library's Result type, the changes aim to improve the robustness, predictability, and clarity of pricing data fetching and calculation, particularly in scenarios involving network failures and fallback to cached data.
Highlights

Consistent Error Handling: The PricingFetcher class and its consumers now consistently utilize the byethrow library's Result type (aliased as R) for all asynchronous operations, making error paths explicit in type signatures.
Functional Error Flow: Key methods within PricingFetcher such as loadOfflinePricing, handleFallbackToCachedPricing, ensurePricingLoaded, fetchModelPricing, getModelPricing, and calculateCostFromTokens have been refactored to leverage R.pipe and other Result operators. This transforms imperative error handling into a more declarative and composable functional pipeline.
Improved Fallback Mechanism: The logic for falling back to cached pricing data when network fetches fail has been seamlessly integrated into the ensurePricingLoaded method using R.orElse, ensuring a robust and graceful recovery mechanism.
Enhanced Code Clarity: By explicitly modeling success and failure states with Result types, the codebase becomes more predictable and easier to reason about, reducing the potential for unhandled exceptions and improving overall maintainability.

TypeScript with strict mode and bundler module resolution
Use .ts extensions for local file imports (e.g., import { foo } from './utils.ts')
Prefer @praha/byethrow Result type over traditional try-catch for functional error handling
Use Result.try() for wrapping operations that may throw (JSON parsing, etc.)
Use Result.isFailure() for checking errors (more readable than !Result.isSuccess())
Use early return pattern (if (Result.isFailure(result)) continue;) instead of ternary operators
For async operations: create wrapper function with Result.try() then call it
Keep traditional try-catch only for: file I/O with complex error handling, legacy code that's hard to refactor
Always use Result.isFailure() and Result.isSuccess() type guards for better code clarity
Variables: start with lowercase (camelCase) - e.g., usageDataSchema, modelBreakdownSchema
Types: start with uppercase (PascalCase) - e.g., UsageData, ModelBreakdown
Constants: can use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE - e.g., DEFAULT_CLAUDE_CODE_PATH
Only export constants, functions, and types that are actually used by other modules
Internal/private constants that are only used within the same file should NOT be exported
Always check if a constant is used elsewhere before making it export const vs just const
Model Naming Convention: Pattern is claude-{model-type}-{generation}-{date} (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-20250514), generation number comes AFTER the model type
Tests are written directly in the same files as the source code, not in separate test files, using if (import.meta.vitest != null) blocks
Vitest globals (describe, it, expect) are available automatically without imports
Dynamic imports using await import() should only be used within test blocks to avoid tree-shaking issues

Test coverage should include both Sonnet and Opus models for comprehensive validation
Model names in tests must exactly match LiteLLM's pricing database entries
When adding new model tests, verify the model exists in LiteLLM before implementation

node_title: refactor: Improve the error handling of the PricingFetcher class
node_bodyText:
Overview
Improved error handling in the PricingFetcher class to implement more robust and consistent error processing. By leveraging the Result type from @praha/byethrow, error propagation and handling have become safer and more predictable.
Key Changes

Introduction of the Result pattern: All asynchronous operations are wrapped in the Result type for explicit error handling
Enhanced type safety: Changed method return types to R.ResultAsync<T, E>
Error propagation: Adopted a functional programming style for error handling using R.pipe()
Other updates: Refactored processes dependent on the PricingFetcher class


Summary by CodeRabbit

Refactor

Enhanced error handling and consistency in pricing and data loading features with a new functional approach.
Improved reliability in cost calculation and model pricing retrieval logic.


Chores

Updated development dependencies to the latest versions for improved stability.

52-601: Configure ESLint to recognize @praha/byethrow patterns
We’re seeing a slew of @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-* false positives because ESLint isn’t aware of the functional types from @praha/byethrow. To address this, update your eslint.config.js to include the MCP plugin for Byethrow:
• In eslint.config.js, add the plugin and recommended config from @praha/byethrow-mcp:
module.exports = {
  // …
  extends: [
+   'plugin:@praha/byethrow-mcp/recommended',
    // your other extends…
  ],
  plugins: [
+   '@praha/byethrow-mcp',
    // your other plugins…
  ],
  // …
};
• If you need finer control, use an override for your TS files to disable or adjust the unsafe-operation rules around Byethrow APIs.
This will suppress the false positives and let ESLint understand the Result, try, pipe, etc., from Byethrow.

node_bodyText:
Overview
Improved error handling in the PricingFetcher class to implement more robust and consistent error processing. By leveraging the Result type from @praha/byethrow, error propagation and handling have become safer and more predictable.
Key Changes

Introduction of the Result pattern: All asynchronous operations are wrapped in the Result type for explicit error handling
Enhanced type safety: Changed method return types to R.ResultAsync<T, E>
Error propagation: Adopted a functional programming style for error handling using R.pipe()
Other updates: Refactored processes dependent on the PricingFetcher class


Summary by CodeRabbit

Refactor

Enhanced error handling and consistency in pricing and data loading features with a new functional approach.
Improved reliability in cost calculation and model pricing retrieval logic.


Chores

Updated development dependencies to the latest versions for improved stability.

node_title: Add HTTP proxy support for network-restricted environments
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR adds transparent HTTP/HTTPS proxy support to ccusage, enabling users in corporate networks or regions with restricted internet access (such as China) to use the tool through proxy servers like Clash Verge or corporate proxies.
Features

Zero external dependencies - Uses only Node.js built-in modules
Automatic proxy detection - Reads from standard environment variables
Authentication support - Username/password proxy authentication
Graceful fallback - Falls back to direct connection if proxy fails
Full compatibility - Complete Fetch API Response object implementation
Comprehensive testing - 12 unit tests covering all scenarios

Implementation
The implementation uses dependency injection with an HttpClient interface, maintaining full backward compatibility. The core components are:

src/http/client.ts - HTTP client interface definitions
src/http/proxy-aware-client.ts - Zero-dependency proxy implementation
src/http/index.ts - Factory functions and exports
Updated src/pricing-fetcher.ts and src/_macro.ts for integration

Usage
Users can configure proxies using standard environment variables:
export HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897

# With authentication
export HTTP_PROXY=http://username:password@proxy.company.com:8080

# Then use ccusage normally
ccusage daily
Benefits

Chinese users can now use ccusage through tools like Clash Verge
Corporate users can use ccusage behind company firewalls
Transparent integration - no changes needed to existing workflows
Maintains project philosophy - zero external dependencies, ultra-small bundle

Testing
All tests pass including 12 new proxy-specific tests covering:

Environment variable detection and parsing
Proxy authentication handling
Error scenarios and graceful fallback
Security considerations (credential protection)

The implementation is production-ready and fully backward compatible.

Summary by CodeRabbit

New Features

Added automatic HTTP/HTTPS proxy support with environment variable detection and authentication.
Requests now gracefully fall back to direct connections on proxy failure, displaying warnings.


Documentation

Added a detailed HTTP Proxy Support section to the configuration guide with usage examples and scenarios.


Refactor

Network requests updated to use a customizable HTTP client for enhanced proxy support and flexibility.

node_title: Add HTTP proxy support for network-restricted environments
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR adds transparent HTTP/HTTPS proxy support to ccusage, enabling users in corporate networks or regions with restricted internet access (such as China) to use the tool through proxy servers like Clash Verge or corporate proxies.
Features

Zero external dependencies - Uses only Node.js built-in modules
Automatic proxy detection - Reads from standard environment variables
Authentication support - Username/password proxy authentication
Graceful fallback - Falls back to direct connection if proxy fails
Full compatibility - Complete Fetch API Response object implementation
Comprehensive testing - 12 unit tests covering all scenarios

Implementation
The implementation uses dependency injection with an HttpClient interface, maintaining full backward compatibility. The core components are:

src/http/client.ts - HTTP client interface definitions
src/http/proxy-aware-client.ts - Zero-dependency proxy implementation
src/http/index.ts - Factory functions and exports
Updated src/pricing-fetcher.ts and src/_macro.ts for integration

Usage
Users can configure proxies using standard environment variables:
export HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:7897

# With authentication
export HTTP_PROXY=http://username:password@proxy.company.com:8080

# Then use ccusage normally
ccusage daily
Benefits

Chinese users can now use ccusage through tools like Clash Verge
Corporate users can use ccusage behind company firewalls
Transparent integration - no changes needed to existing workflows
Maintains project philosophy - zero external dependencies, ultra-small bundle

Testing
All tests pass including 12 new proxy-specific tests covering:

Environment variable detection and parsing
Proxy authentication handling
Error scenarios and graceful fallback
Security considerations (credential protection)

The implementation is production-ready and fully backward compatible.

Summary by CodeRabbit

New Features

Added automatic HTTP/HTTPS proxy support with environment variable detection and authentication.
Requests now gracefully fall back to direct connections on proxy failure, displaying warnings.


Documentation

Added a detailed HTTP Proxy Support section to the configuration guide with usage examples and scenarios.


Refactor

Network requests updated to use a customizable HTTP client for enhanced proxy support and flexibility.

node_title: fix: improve error handling for cloud sync ENOENT errors
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR improves error handling for cloud synchronization scenarios where JSONL files may be temporarily unavailable due to ongoing sync operations.
Changes

Enhanced live monitoring error handling: Added specific detection and handling for ENOENT errors in _blocks.live.ts
User-friendly messaging: Display warning instead of error for sync-related issues with helpful context
Improved logging: Use debug level for temporary file unavailability to reduce log noise
Better error preservation: Maintain original error information for debugging while handling gracefully
Continue monitoring: ENOENT errors now show warning and continue monitoring instead of terminating the program

Problem Solved
Fixes #246 - Users syncing Claude data directories via cloud storage (like Nutstore) would see error messages when files were temporarily unavailable during sync. This fix makes the tool more resilient to such scenarios by continuing to monitor instead of exiting.
Key Improvements

No program termination: ENOENT errors during cloud sync no longer cause the live monitoring to exit
Graceful recovery: Program automatically recovers when sync completes
Better user experience: Clear warning messages with helpful context
Persistent monitoring: Continues checking for data availability during sync operations

Testing
The changes maintain existing functionality while gracefully handling file access errors. Error handling uses the existing Result.try pattern for consistency. Non-sync errors will still properly terminate the program as expected.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Improved error messages and warnings for file synchronization issues, providing clearer feedback when files are temporarily unavailable due to syncing.



Bug Fixes

Enhanced error handling to better distinguish between file sync errors and other issues, ensuring appropriate logging and user notifications.



Style

Updated session time displays in live monitoring to show hours and minutes (e.g., "1h 23m") instead of compact millisecond-based formats for improved readability.

node_title: fix: improve error handling for cloud sync ENOENT errors
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR improves error handling for cloud synchronization scenarios where JSONL files may be temporarily unavailable due to ongoing sync operations.
Changes

Enhanced live monitoring error handling: Added specific detection and handling for ENOENT errors in _blocks.live.ts
User-friendly messaging: Display warning instead of error for sync-related issues with helpful context
Improved logging: Use debug level for temporary file unavailability to reduce log noise
Better error preservation: Maintain original error information for debugging while handling gracefully
Continue monitoring: ENOENT errors now show warning and continue monitoring instead of terminating the program

Problem Solved
Fixes #246 - Users syncing Claude data directories via cloud storage (like Nutstore) would see error messages when files were temporarily unavailable during sync. This fix makes the tool more resilient to such scenarios by continuing to monitor instead of exiting.
Key Improvements

No program termination: ENOENT errors during cloud sync no longer cause the live monitoring to exit
Graceful recovery: Program automatically recovers when sync completes
Better user experience: Clear warning messages with helpful context
Persistent monitoring: Continues checking for data availability during sync operations

Testing
The changes maintain existing functionality while gracefully handling file access errors. Error handling uses the existing Result.try pattern for consistency. Non-sync errors will still properly terminate the program as expected.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Improved error messages and warnings for file synchronization issues, providing clearer feedback when files are temporarily unavailable due to syncing.



Bug Fixes

Enhanced error handling to better distinguish between file sync errors and other issues, ensuring appropriate logging and user notifications.



Style

Updated session time displays in live monitoring to show hours and minutes (e.g., "1h 23m") instead of compact millisecond-based formats for improved readability.

The error handling has multiple issues that were previously flagged by other reviewers:

+	catch (error) {
+		// Handle file access errors gracefully
+		// This ensures files without timestamps or with access issues are sorted to the end
+
+		// Check if this is a file sync related error (ENOENT)
+		const isEnoent = error instanceof Error
+			&& 'code' in error
+			&& (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT';
+
+		if (isEnoent) {
+			// For ENOENT errors (likely due to cloud sync), use debug level to avoid spam
+			logger.debug(`File temporarily unavailable (likely syncing): ${path.basename(filePath)}`);
+		}
+		else {
+			// For other errors, log with more detail for debugging
+			logger.debug(`Failed to get earliest timestamp for ${filePath}:`, error);
+		}
+
		return null;
	}

97-113: Consider using the Result pattern for consistency.
While the current approach using traditional try-catch is acceptable per the coding guidelines for file I/O operations, consider using the Result pattern for consistency with the codebase. This would align with the guidelines that prefer @praha/byethrow Result type and use Result.try() for operations that may throw.
Here's how you could refactor using the Result pattern:
-			for (const file of sortedFiles) {
-				const content = await readFile(file, 'utf-8')
-					.catch((error) => {
-						// Handle file access errors gracefully with specific logging for ENOENT
-						const isEnoent = error instanceof Error
-							&& 'code' in error
-							&& (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT';
-
-						if (isEnoent) {
-							// For ENOENT errors (likely due to cloud sync), use debug level

-						}
-						else {
-							// For other read errors, use debug level but with more detail
-							logger.debug(`Failed to read usage file ${path.basename(file)}:`, error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
-						}
-
-						// Skip files that can't be read
-						return '';
-					});
+			for (const file of sortedFiles) {
+				const fileReader = Result.try({
+					try: async () => readFile(file, 'utf-8'),
+					catch: (error) => {
+						// Preserve original error information for better debugging
+						if (error instanceof Error) {
+							return error;
+						}
+						return new Error(`File read failed: ${String(error)}`);
+					},
+				});
+
+				const fileResult = await fileReader();
+				if (Result.isFailure(fileResult)) {
+					// Handle file access errors gracefully with specific logging for ENOENT
+					const error = fileResult.error;
+					const isEnoent = 'code' in error && (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT';
+
+					if (isEnoent) {
+						// For ENOENT errors (likely due to cloud sync), use debug level
+						logger.debug(`File temporarily unavailable (likely syncing): ${path.basename(file)}`);
+					}
+					else {
+						// For other read errors, use debug level but with more detail
+						logger.debug(`Failed to read usage file ${path.basename(file)}:`, error.message);
+					}
+					continue;
+				}
+
+				const content = fileResult.value;
This approach would require keeping the Result import and would be more consistent with the codebase patterns.

node_title: fix: improve error handling for cloud sync ENOENT errors
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR improves error handling for cloud synchronization scenarios where JSONL files may be temporarily unavailable due to ongoing sync operations.
Changes

Enhanced live monitoring error handling: Added specific detection and handling for ENOENT errors in _blocks.live.ts
User-friendly messaging: Display warning instead of error for sync-related issues with helpful context
Improved logging: Use debug level for temporary file unavailability to reduce log noise
Better error preservation: Maintain original error information for debugging while handling gracefully
Continue monitoring: ENOENT errors now show warning and continue monitoring instead of terminating the program

Problem Solved
Fixes #246 - Users syncing Claude data directories via cloud storage (like Nutstore) would see error messages when files were temporarily unavailable during sync. This fix makes the tool more resilient to such scenarios by continuing to monitor instead of exiting.
Key Improvements

No program termination: ENOENT errors during cloud sync no longer cause the live monitoring to exit
Graceful recovery: Program automatically recovers when sync completes
Better user experience: Clear warning messages with helpful context
Persistent monitoring: Continues checking for data availability during sync operations

Testing
The changes maintain existing functionality while gracefully handling file access errors. Error handling uses the existing Result.try pattern for consistency. Non-sync errors will still properly terminate the program as expected.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Improved error messages and warnings for file synchronization issues, providing clearer feedback when files are temporarily unavailable due to syncing.



Bug Fixes

Enhanced error handling to better distinguish between file sync errors and other issues, ensuring appropriate logging and user notifications.



Style

Updated session time displays in live monitoring to show hours and minutes (e.g., "1h 23m") instead of compact millisecond-based formats for improved readability.

Summary of Changes
Hello @jaried, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request significantly improves the user experience of the live monitoring feature by providing more precise and readable time displays. It also enhances the robustness of the monitoring process by introducing sophisticated error handling for file access, especially in scenarios involving cloud synchronization, ensuring a more stable and informative user interface.
Highlights

Improved Time Precision: I've enhanced the live monitoring display (ccusage blocks --live) to show time with minute-level accuracy, moving beyond the previous hour-only precision.
Standardized Time Format: The prettyMs compact format for displaying elapsed and remaining time has been replaced with a more explicit Xh Ym format, ensuring consistency and clarity across the live monitoring interface.
Enhanced Compact Display: In the compact terminal mode, the remaining time is now displayed on a separate line, improving visibility and readability for users.
Robust File Access Error Handling: I've implemented more graceful error handling for file access issues, particularly for ENOENT errors which often occur due to cloud synchronization. The system now logs these specific errors at a debug level and provides a user-friendly warning message, allowing live monitoring to continue without crashing.

node_title: feat(i18n): Implement internationalization support
node_bodyText:
Add Full Internationalization (i18n) Support
Overview
This pull request implements comprehensive internationalization (i18n) support throughout the ccusage CLI tool. All user-facing strings—including table headers, error messages, and status information—are now fully translatable. The CLI detects the system locale or accepts a language override via the --lang option.
Technical Details


Locale Detection:

The CLI checks for a --lang CLI argument, then falls back to environment variables (LANG, LC_ALL, LANGUAGE), and defaults to English if none are set.
Supported languages: English (en), French (fr), Spanish (es), German (de), Japanese (ja), Chinese (zh).



Translation Architecture:

All translations are stored in JSON files under locales (e.g., en.json, fr.json, etc.).
The i18n module loads the appropriate translation file at runtime and falls back to English for missing keys.
Parameter interpolation is supported for dynamic values within translation strings.



TypeScript & ESLint Compliance:

All code now uses strict null checks and explicit type annotations.
Unsafe any usage has been eliminated; all object accesses are type-safe.
All conditional checks on possibly-null or undefined values are explicit.
ESLint errors and warnings have been resolved across the codebase.



CLI Integration:

The language can be set via --lang or -l (e.g., ccusage --lang=fr).
All commands and output (including live monitoring, error messages, and help text) are localized.



Validation & Tooling:

Added and improved translation validation scripts to ensure all locale files are complete and consistent.
The validation script checks for missing, extra, or empty keys and placeholder values.



Documentation:

The README and i18n guide have been updated with usage instructions and language examples.
Markdown code blocks in documentation have been adjusted to avoid ESLint parsing errors.



Motivation
This update makes ccusage accessible to a global audience, ensures robust and maintainable code, and provides a scalable foundation for future language additions.

Summary by CodeRabbit

Added full internationalization (i18n) support with multilingual CLI output and reports in English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, and Chinese.
Introduced a --lang option and automatic locale detection for user-facing text.

Currency formatting and live monitoring UI are adapted to the selected language.



Documentation

Updated README with internationalization details and usage examples.
Added a comprehensive Internationalization Guide covering language selection, translation coverage, and troubleshooting.



Chores

Added translation validation scripts and npm tasks to ensure translation completeness and consistency.
Included new translation files for all supported languages.

The language can be set via --lang or -l (e.g., ccusage --lang=fr).
All commands and output (including live monitoring, error messages, and help text) are localized.



Validation & Tooling:

Added and improved translation validation scripts to ensure all locale files are complete and consistent.
The validation script checks for missing, extra, or empty keys and placeholder values.



Documentation:

The README and i18n guide have been updated with usage instructions and language examples.
Markdown code blocks in documentation have been adjusted to avoid ESLint parsing errors.



Motivation
This update makes ccusage accessible to a global audience, ensures robust and maintainable code, and provides a scalable foundation for future language additions.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added full internationalization (i18n) support with multilingual CLI output and reports in English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, and Chinese.
Introduced a --lang option and automatic locale detection for user-facing text.
All command descriptions, error messages, table headers, and reports are now localized.
Currency formatting and live monitoring UI are adapted to the selected language.



Documentation

Updated README with internationalization details and usage examples.
Added a comprehensive Internationalization Guide covering language selection, translation coverage, and troubleshooting.



Chores

Added translation validation scripts and npm tasks to ensure translation completeness and consistency.
Included new translation files for all supported languages.

68-75: Simplify the null/undefined check.
The condition is overly verbose. Since headerMapping[header] can only return string | undefined, checking for undefined is sufficient.
-		return headers.map((header) => {
-			const translationKey = headerMapping[header];
-			if (translationKey !== undefined && translationKey !== null && translationKey !== '') {
-				return i18n.t(translationKey);
-			}

+			const translationKey = headerMapping[header];

+				return i18n.t(translationKey);
+			}
+			// Return original header if no translation found
+			return header;
+		});

83-86: Simplify the compactHead translation logic.
The null/undefined checks are redundant, and the ternary operator can be simplified.
-		// Translate headers automatically
-		this.head = this.translateHeaders(options.head);

55-74: Simplify the locale validation checks.
The null/undefined/empty string checks are overly verbose and can be simplified using modern JavaScript operators.
-		// If CLI argument provided (not 'auto'), use it
-		if (cliLocale !== undefined && cliLocale !== null && cliLocale !== '' && cliLocale !== 'auto' && this.isValidLocale(cliLocale)) {
-			return cliLocale as Locale;
-		}
+		// If CLI argument provided (not 'auto'), use it
+		if (cliLocale && cliLocale !== 'auto' && this.isValidLocale(cliLocale)) {

-		// Try environment variables

-		if (envLang !== undefined && envLang !== null && envLang !== '') {

-				return langCode as Locale;

+		// Try environment variables
+		const envLang = process.env.LANG ?? process.env.LC_ALL ?? process.env.LANGUAGE;
+		if (envLang) {
+			// Extract language code (e.g., 'fr_FR.UTF-8' -> 'fr')
+			const langCode = envLang.split(/[_.-]/)[0]?.toLowerCase();
+			if (langCode && this.isValidLocale(langCode)) {
+				return langCode as Locale;
+			}
+		}

139-144: Simplify null checks in getTranslation.
The null check can be simplified using modern operators.
-		const targetLocale = locale !== undefined && locale !== null ? locale : this.currentLocale;
-		const translations = this.translations.get(targetLocale) !== undefined ? this.translations.get(targetLocale)! : this.fallbackTranslations;
+		const targetLocale = locale ?? this.currentLocale;
+		const translations = this.translations.get(targetLocale) ?? this.fallbackTranslations;

177-194: Simplify empty string checks in translation method.
The null/undefined/empty string checks can be simplified.
-		// Fallback to English if not found
-		if ((translation === undefined || translation === null || translation === '') && this.currentLocale !== 'en') {
-			translation = this.getTranslation(key, 'en');
-		}
-
-		// If still not found, return the key itself as fallback

-			logger.warn(`Translation not found for key: ${key}`);
-			return key;
-		}
+		// Fallback to English if not found
+		if (!translation && this.currentLocale !== 'en') {
+			translation = this.getTranslation(key, 'en');
+		}
+
+		// If still not found, return the key itself as fallback
+		if (!translation) {
+			logger.warn(`Translation not found for key: ${key}`);
+			return key;
+		}

250-261: Simplify null checks in getTranslationWithParams.

-			return key; // Return key if translation not found

Prefer @praha/byethrow Result type over traditional try-catch for functional error handling
Use Result.try() for wrapping operations that may throw (JSON parsing, etc.)
Use Result.isFailure() for checking errors (more readable than !Result.isSuccess())
Use early return pattern (if (Result.isFailure(result)) continue;) instead of ternary operators

Keep traditional try-catch only for: file I/O with complex error handling, legacy code that's hard to refactor

node_title: feat(i18n): Implement internationalization support
node_bodyText:
Add Full Internationalization (i18n) Support
Overview
This pull request implements comprehensive internationalization (i18n) support throughout the ccusage CLI tool. All user-facing strings—including table headers, error messages, and status information—are now fully translatable. The CLI detects the system locale or accepts a language override via the --lang option.
Technical Details


Locale Detection:

The CLI checks for a --lang CLI argument, then falls back to environment variables (LANG, LC_ALL, LANGUAGE), and defaults to English if none are set.
Supported languages: English (en), French (fr), Spanish (es), German (de), Japanese (ja), Chinese (zh).



Translation Architecture:

All translations are stored in JSON files under locales (e.g., en.json, fr.json, etc.).
The i18n module loads the appropriate translation file at runtime and falls back to English for missing keys.
Parameter interpolation is supported for dynamic values within translation strings.



TypeScript & ESLint Compliance:

All code now uses strict null checks and explicit type annotations.
Unsafe any usage has been eliminated; all object accesses are type-safe.
All conditional checks on possibly-null or undefined values are explicit.
ESLint errors and warnings have been resolved across the codebase.



CLI Integration:

The language can be set via --lang or -l (e.g., ccusage --lang=fr).
All commands and output (including live monitoring, error messages, and help text) are localized.



Validation & Tooling:

Added and improved translation validation scripts to ensure all locale files are complete and consistent.
The validation script checks for missing, extra, or empty keys and placeholder values.



Documentation:

The README and i18n guide have been updated with usage instructions and language examples.
Markdown code blocks in documentation have been adjusted to avoid ESLint parsing errors.



Motivation
This update makes ccusage accessible to a global audience, ensures robust and maintainable code, and provides a scalable foundation for future language additions.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added full internationalization (i18n) support with multilingual CLI output and reports in English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, and Chinese.
Introduced a --lang option and automatic locale detection for user-facing text.
All command descriptions, error messages, table headers, and reports are now localized.
Currency formatting and live monitoring UI are adapted to the selected language.



Documentation

Updated README with internationalization details and usage examples.
Added a comprehensive Internationalization Guide covering language selection, translation coverage, and troubleshooting.



Chores

Added translation validation scripts and npm tasks to ensure translation completeness and consistency.
Included new translation files for all supported languages.

+	const projBarPadded = projBarStr + ' '.repeat(Math.max(0, boxWidth - 3 - stringWidth(projBarStr)));
+	terminal.write(`${marginStr}│ ${projBarPadded}│\n`);
+
+	// Projection details (indented and aligned)
+	const col1 = `${pc.gray('Status:')} ${limitStatus}`;
+	const col2 = isCostMode 
+		? `${pc.gray('Cost:')} ${formatCurrency(projection.totalCost)}`
+		: `${pc.gray('Tokens:')} ${formatNumber(projection.totalTokens)}`;
+	const col3 = isCostMode
+		? `${pc.gray('Tokens:')} ${formatNumber(projection.totalTokens)}`
+		: `${pc.gray('Cost:')} ${formatCurrency(projection.totalCost)}`;
+	
+	// Calculate visible lengths (without ANSI codes)
+	const col1Visible = stringWidth(col1);
+	const col2Visible = stringWidth(col2);
+	// Fixed column positions - match session alignment
+	const pad1 = ' '.repeat(Math.max(0, DETAIL_COLUMN_WIDTHS.col1 - col1Visible));
+	const pad2 = ' '.repeat(Math.max(0, DETAIL_COLUMN_WIDTHS.col2 - col2Visible));
+	const projDetails = `   ${col1}${pad1}${col2}${pad2}${col3}`;
+	const projDetailsPadded = projDetails + ' '.repeat(Math.max(0, boxWidth - 3 - stringWidth(projDetails)));
+	terminal.write(`${marginStr}│ ${projDetailsPadded}│\n`);
+}

node_bodyText:
Add new cost limit functionality for live monitoring mode:

Add -c/--cost-limit argument supporting numeric values and "max" keyword
Implement cost-based progress bars and projections in live display
Add mutual exclusivity validation between token and cost limits
Support cost burn rate display ($X.XX/hour) instead of tokens/min
Add maxCostFromAll calculation to find highest cost from previous sessions
Update live rendering to show cost-focused displays when cost limit is active
Maintain backward compatibility with existing token-based monitoring

Technical changes:

Add parseCostLimit() function mirroring parseTokenLimit() logic
Extend LiveMonitoringConfig type with costLimit field
Update compact display mode to support cost limits
Add comprehensive test coverage for cost limit scenarios
Create BUILD.md with local installation and development instructions

Breaking changes: None - fully backward compatible

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added support for cost-based limits and per-model filtering in live usage monitoring, enabling more flexible and precise tracking.
Introduced ranked limit parsing for token and cost limits, including support for "2nd-max", "3rd-max", etc.
Added model filtering options to commands and live monitoring to focus on specific models.
Enhanced burn rate calculations with activity density for sparse usage, improving projection accuracy.



Documentation

Added a comprehensive BUILD.md file with detailed instructions for building, installing, developing, and troubleshooting the project locally.



Style

Updated the live monitoring header to reflect broader usage monitoring beyond just tokens.



Chores

Updated the package name for global installation and testing purposes.

node_title: feat(blocks): add cost-based and model based live monitoring support
node_bodyText:
feat(blocks): add cost-based live monitoring with -c/--cost-limit option
Add new cost limit functionality for live monitoring mode:

Add -c/--cost-limit argument supporting numeric values and "max" keyword
Implement cost-based progress bars and projections in live display
Add mutual exclusivity validation between token and cost limits
Support cost burn rate display ($X.XX/hour) instead of tokens/min
Add maxCostFromAll calculation to find highest cost from previous sessions
Update live rendering to show cost-focused displays when cost limit is active
Maintain backward compatibility with existing token-based monitoring

Technical changes:

Add parseCostLimit() function mirroring parseTokenLimit() logic
Extend LiveMonitoringConfig type with costLimit field
Update compact display mode to support cost limits
Add comprehensive test coverage for cost limit scenarios
Create BUILD.md with local installation and development instructions

Breaking changes: None - fully backward compatible
feat(blocks): add model filtering support with -m/--model option
Add CLI support for filtering usage data by specific Claude models in blocks command.
Supports both static and live monitoring modes with partial model name matching.
Changes:

Add -m/--model CLI argument accepting comma-separated model names
Update LoadOptions interface to include models filter
Implement model filtering in loadSessionBlockData with partial matching
Add model filtering to LiveMonitor for live mode support
Update LiveMonitoringConfig interface to pass model filter
Support partial matching (e.g., "sonnet" matches "claude-sonnet-4-20250514")

Usage examples:

ccusage blocks --model sonnet
ccusage blocks --model sonnet,opus
ccusage blocks --live --model sonnet


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added support for cost-based usage limits and live monitoring, allowing users to set and track cost limits in addition to token limits.
Introduced model filtering capabilities, enabling users to filter usage data and statistics by specific model names.
Added per-model cost limit functionality and detailed per-model usage breakdowns.
Improved activity-aware projections for more accurate usage forecasting.



Documentation

Added a comprehensive build and installation guide, including troubleshooting tips and descriptions of new features.



Chores

Updated the package name to "hg-ccusage" for distribution.
bodyText:
Summary of Changes
Hello @hitesh-goel, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request significantly expands the capabilities of the blocks command by introducing robust cost-based live monitoring and granular model filtering. It allows users to track and project their Claude usage by cost, alongside existing token metrics, and to focus on specific models. These new features are supported by more intelligent limit calculations and improved projection accuracy, all while enhancing the overall development and testing experience with new documentation.
Highlights

Cost-Based Live Monitoring: I've added a new --cost-limit option to the blocks command for live monitoring. This allows users to track and project their usage based on monetary cost, complete with cost-focused progress bars, burn rate display ($/hour), and projections. It maintains backward compatibility with existing token-based monitoring.
Model Filtering Support: The blocks command now supports filtering usage data by specific Claude models using the new -m/--model CLI argument. This works in both static and live monitoring modes and supports partial model name matching.
Intelligent Limit Calculation: The 'max' keyword for both token and cost limits has been enhanced. It now calculates the highest historical usage (tokens or cost) on a per-model basis, providing more accurate and relevant limits, especially when filtering by specific models.
Improved Live Monitoring Projections: To provide more realistic usage projections, I've introduced an 'activity density' metric. This helps adjust projections for sparse or intermittent usage patterns, preventing overestimation of future consumption.
Enhanced Development Experience: A comprehensive BUILD.md guide has been added to simplify local development, building, and testing. It includes instructions for using custom package names, development links, and detailed troubleshooting.
