node_title: fix: Windows hang when CWD contains symbolic links
node_bodyText:
Problem
ccusage would hang indefinitely on Windows when run from directories containing symbolic links (junction points) such as:

C:\Users\{username}\Documents (contains My Music, My Pictures, My Videos junctions)
C:\Users\{username} (contains My Documents, Application Data, etc.)

This issue was discovered through https://github.com/Owloops/claude-powerline which uses ccusage's loadSessionUsageById() function and would hang when run from these directories.
Root Cause
The issue is ultimately caused by a bug in tinyglobby where Windows absolute paths with backslashes (e.g., C:\Users\...\**\file.jsonl) would cause the glob function to incorrectly process the path when the current working directory contained symbolic links.
Solution
Convert backslashes to forward slashes in glob patterns. Forward slashes are cross-platform compatible and avoid the tinyglobby bug entirely.
Changes

Modified loadSessionUsageById in src/data-loader.ts to replace backslashes with forward slashes in the glob pattern

Testing
Tested the following scenarios on Windows:

This PR implements dynamic context limits for Claude models, replacing the hardcoded 200K limit with model-specific limits fetched from LiteLLM data.

Enhanced Type Safety: Add context limit fields to modelPricingSchema
Improved Statusline: Pass model ID to enable dynamic context percentage calculation
Comprehensive Testing: Add test fixtures and commands for Claude 4 model variants
Code Quality: Remove inappropriate test code from command files, maintain clean separation of concerns

PricingFetcher.getModelContextLimit() - Retrieve model-specific context limits
calculateContextTokens() - Accept modelId parameter for dynamic limit lookup
Fallback to 200K limit when model data unavailable for backward compatibility
Proper error handling and logging for context limit retrieval

Enhanced ESLint compliance with proper TypeScript private property access
Maintained separation of concerns - commands focus on execution, tests belong in appropriate modules

Add comprehensive unit tests

Remove inappropriate test code from statusline command
Fix TypeScript private property access in tests
Use shortened ESLint rule names for consistency

node_title: feat(statusline): fetching context limit per model dynamically from litellm
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR implements dynamic context limits for Claude models, replacing the hardcoded 200K limit with model-specific limits fetched from LiteLLM data.
Key Changes

Dynamic Context Calculation: Replace fixed CONTEXT_LIMIT constant with model-specific limits
LiteLLM Integration: Fetch context limits from LiteLLM pricing data (max_input_tokens or max_tokens)
Enhanced Type Safety: Add context limit fields to modelPricingSchema
Improved Statusline: Pass model ID to enable dynamic context percentage calculation
Comprehensive Testing: Add test fixtures and commands for Claude 4 model variants
Code Quality: Remove inappropriate test code from command files, maintain clean separation of concerns

Technical Implementation

PricingFetcher.getModelContextLimit() - Retrieve model-specific context limits
calculateContextTokens() - Accept modelId parameter for dynamic limit lookup
Fallback to 200K limit when model data unavailable for backward compatibility
Proper error handling and logging for context limit retrieval

Code Quality Improvements

Removed inappropriate test logic from statusline command file
Enhanced ESLint compliance with proper TypeScript private property access
Maintained separation of concerns - commands focus on execution, tests belong in appropriate modules
All quality checks pass: lint, typecheck, and build successful

Testing
New test commands added:

bun run test:statusline:sonnet4 - Test with Claude 4 Sonnet
bun run test:statusline:opus4 - Test with Claude 4.1 Opus
bun run test:statusline:sonnet41 - Test with Claude 4.1 Sonnet
bun run test:statusline:all - Run all model tests

Quality Assurance

 ESLint checks pass
 TypeScript compilation successful
 Build process completes without errors
 Unit tests for getModelContextLimit method
 Context percentage calculation tests
 Model-specific test fixtures created
 Manual testing with different Claude 4 models
 Backward compatibility verified
 Clean code architecture maintained

Backward Compatibility

Maintains 200K fallback for unknown models
No breaking changes to existing APIs
All existing functionality preserved

Implementation Details
Commits Summary (11 commits)

Remove hardcoded CONTEXT_LIMIT constant
Add context limit fields to model pricing schema
Add getModelContextLimit method to PricingFetcher
Update statusline to use dynamic context limits
Add Claude 4 model test commands
Add test data files for Claude 4 variants
Add comprehensive unit tests
Update lsmcp memory with feature documentation
Remove inappropriate test code from statusline command
Fix TypeScript private property access in tests
Use shortened ESLint rule names for consistency

This feature enables accurate, model-specific context usage reporting while maintaining excellent code quality and comprehensive test coverage.

🔭 Outside diff range comments (1)

src/commands/statusline.ts (1)
166-191: Resolve ts/no-unsafe- and avoid shadowing; locally narrow types for calculateContextTokens() call*
ESLint is flagging multiple ts/no-unsafe-* violations on Line 169 due to:

Accessing hookData fields without a narrowed type in this scope
Accessing ctx.values.offline where ctx is untyped in this command’s run() signature
Additionally, the map callback parameter named ctx shadows the outer command context, hurting readability.

Locally narrow the types we need, coerce offline to a boolean, and avoid the shadowed identifier.
Apply this diff:
 		// Calculate context tokens from transcript with model-specific limits
-		const contextInfo = await Result.pipe(
+		// Narrow types locally to satisfy eslint ts/no-unsafe-* without impacting outer scope
+		type MinimalHookData = { transcript_path: string; model: { id?: string } };
+		const { transcript_path, model } = hookData as MinimalHookData;
+		const offline = Boolean((ctx as { values?: { offline?: unknown } }).values?.offline);
+
+		const contextInfo = await Result.pipe(
 			Result.try({
-				try: calculateContextTokens(hookData.transcript_path, hookData.model.id, ctx.values.offline),
+				try: calculateContextTokens(transcript_path, model.id, offline),
 				catch: error => error,
 			}),
 			Result.inspectError(error => logger.debug(`Failed to calculate context tokens: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`)),
-			Result.map((ctx) => {
-				if (ctx == null) {
+			Result.map((info) => {
+				if (info == null) {
 					return undefined;
 				}
 				// Format context percentage with color coding using configurable thresholds
 				const thresholds = getContextUsageThresholds();
-				const color = ctx.percentage < thresholds.LOW
+				const color = info.percentage < thresholds.LOW
 					? pc.green
-					: ctx.percentage < thresholds.MEDIUM
+					: info.percentage < thresholds.MEDIUM
 						? pc.yellow
 						: pc.red;
-				const coloredPercentage = color(`${ctx.percentage}%`);
+				const coloredPercentage = color(`${info.percentage}%`);
 
 				// Format token count with thousand separators
-				const tokenDisplay = ctx.inputTokens.toLocaleString();
+				const tokenDisplay = info.inputTokens.toLocaleString();
 				return `${tokenDisplay} (${coloredPercentage})`;
 			}),
 			Result.unwrap(undefined),
 		);

48-55: Wrap JSON.parse in Result.try() to match guidelines and avoid hard exits on parse errors
JSON.parse can throw; current code will crash before zod validation can produce a cleaner message. Per the repo’s guidelines, prefer Result.try() for operations that may throw.
Example adjustment (outside the changed hunk; illustrative snippet):
// Read input from stdin
const stdin = await getStdin();

node_title: feat(statusline): Add visual burn rate indicators to statusline for improved accessibility
node_bodyText:
Problem
The statusline command uses color-only indicators to show burn rate status (green for normal, yellow for moderate, red for high).
This creates accessibility issues in environments where:

Shells don't support color output
Color output is standardized/stripped
Users have color vision deficiencies
Terminal configurations don't display colors properly

Solution
This PR adds a new --visual-burn-rate option that provides alternative visual indicators beyond color:

off (default): Color-only output (maintains backward compatibility)
emoji: Adds emoji indicators (🟢 Normal, ⚠️ Moderate, 🚨 High)
text: Adds text labels (Normal), (Moderate), (High)
emoji-text: Combines both emoji and text indicators

Changes

Added visualBurnRate argument with enum choices and short flag -vb
Refactored burn rate display logic to support multiple visual indicators
Maintains existing color coding while adding optional visual enhancements
Added proper TypeScript typing for burn status mappings

Examples
Default behavior (color only)
bun run start statusline
Add emoji indicators
bun run start statusline --visual-burn-rate emoji
Add text indicators
bun run start statusline --visual-burn-rate text
Add both emoji and text
bun run start statusline --visual-burn-rate emoji-text
Output Examples

Color only: 🔥 $2.50/hr (with color)
With emoji: 🔥 $2.50/hr 🟢
With text: 🔥 $2.50/hr (Normal)
With both: 🔥 $2.50/hr 🟢 (Normal)

This enhancement improves accessibility while maintaining full backward compatibility.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added a CLI option to control burn-rate visualization in the status line: off (default), emoji, text, or emoji-text (short flag: -vb).
Burn rate now classifies usage into Normal, Moderate, or High and displays colored indicators (green/yellow/red) with optional emoji and/or text alongside cost-per-hour.



Documentation

Added a Visual Burn Rate section with examples; content was inserted twice (duplicate copies).

+											const visualBurnRate = ctx.values.visualBurnRate as VisualBurnRate;
+											const renderEmojiStatus = visualBurnRate === 'emoji' || visualBurnRate === 'emoji-text';
+											const renderTextStatus = visualBurnRate === 'text' || visualBurnRate === 'emoji-text';
Note: I’m purposefully keeping the assertion scoped to this value to avoid bleeding assertions elsewhere. If you’d rather avoid any assertions, a small type guard like function isVisualBurnRate(x: string): x is VisualBurnRate using visualBurnRateChoices.includes(x) would also work.

299-305: Avoid hardcoded thresholds; use canonical BURN_RATE_THRESHOLDS and align comparison direction.
This block re-encodes thresholds (2000/5000) and "<" direction, which has been inconsistent with the canonical constants/logic elsewhere. Import BURN_RATE_THRESHOLDS and use the same ">" direction for consistency and single source of truth.
-											type BurnStatus = 'normal' | 'moderate' | 'high';
+											type BurnStatus = 'normal' | 'moderate' | 'high';
 
-											const burnStatus: BurnStatus = burnRate.tokensPerMinuteForIndicator < 2000
-												? 'normal'
-												: burnRate.tokensPerMinuteForIndicator < 5000
-													? 'moderate'
-													: 'high';
+											const burnStatus: BurnStatus = burnRate.tokensPerMinuteForIndicator > BURN_RATE_THRESHOLDS.HIGH
+												? 'high'
+												: burnRate.tokensPerMinuteForIndicator > BURN_RATE_THRESHOLDS.MODERATE
+													? 'moderate'
+													: 'normal';
And update the import at the top accordingly:
-import { DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS } from '../_consts.ts';
+import { DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS, BURN_RATE_THRESHOLDS } from '../_consts.ts';
If you prefer to keep this PR focused, I can open a follow-up issue to track harmonizing burn-rate thresholds across modules.

307-314: Use satisfies to keep types precise and avoid picocolors typing warnings.
Explicitly annotating the mapping with Record<..., Formatter> is tripping static analysis (pc.* seen as error-typed). The satisfies operator preserves type safety without forcing a type on pc.* functions.
-											const burnStatusMappings: Record<BurnStatus, { emoji: string; textValue: string; coloredString: Formatter }> = {
-												normal: { emoji: '🟢', textValue: 'Normal', coloredString: pc.green },
-												moderate: { emoji: '⚠️', textValue: 'Moderate', coloredString: pc.yellow },
-												high: { emoji: '🚨', textValue: 'High', coloredString: pc.red },
-											};
+											const burnStatusMappings = {
+												normal: { emoji: '🟢', textValue: 'Normal', coloredString: pc.green },
+												moderate: { emoji: '⚠️', textValue: 'Moderate', coloredString: pc.yellow },
+												high: { emoji: '🚨', textValue: 'High', coloredString: pc.red },
+											} satisfies Record<BurnStatus, { emoji: string; textValue: string; coloredString: (s: string) => string }>;
This keeps the same runtime behavior, eliminates the "error type" cascade, and lets you drop the dedicated Formatter import.

1-1: Remove now-unused Formatter import if you adopt the satisfies refactor.
If you switch the mapping to use satisfies with a simple string->string function type, this import becomes unused.

#​10283 80960b9 Thanks @​WillTaylorDev! - Support long branch names in generation of branch aliases in WCI.

#​10232 e7cae16 Thanks @​emily-shen! - fix: validate wrangler containers delete ID to ensure a valid ID has been provided. Previously if you provided the container name (or any non-ID shaped string) you would get an auth error instead of a 404.


#​10139 3b6ab8a Thanks @​dom96! - Removes mention of cf-requirements when Python Workers are enabled


#​10259 c58a05c Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Ensure that maybeStartOrUpdateRemoteProxySession considers the potential account_id from the user's wrangler config
Currently if the user has an account_id in their wrangler config file, such id won't be taken into consideration for the remote proxy session, the changes here make sure that it is (note that the auth option of maybeStartOrUpdateRemoteProxySession, if provided, takes precedence over this id value).
The changes here also fix the same issue for wrangler dev and getPlatformProxy (since they use maybeStartOrUpdateRemoteProxySession under the hook).


#​10288 42aafa3 Thanks @​tgarg-cf! - Do not attempt to update queue producer settings when deploying a Worker with a queue binding
Previously, each deployed Worker would update a subset of the queue producer's settings for each queue binding, which could result in broken queue producers or at least conflicts where different Workers tried to set different producer settings on a shared queue.


#​10242 70bd966 Thanks @​devin-ai-integration! - Add experimental API to expose Wrangler command tree structure for documentation generation

node_title: feat(statusline): implement rate limiting with class-based semaphore
node_bodyText:
Summary
Implements file-based semaphore rate limiting for the statusline command to address issue #459 (process spawning loop causing resource exhaustion).
Key Features

File-based semaphore using @ryoppippi/limo with automatic resource management
Class-based design for reusable rate limiting across commands
1-second default interval unified with live monitoring
Configurable options (--refresh-interval, --disable-cache)
Comprehensive testing with vitest

Technical Implementation

Semaphore files stored in `${os.tmpdir()}/ccusage-statusline/`
Uses Zod schema validation and @praha/byethrow Result type
Automatic cleanup and error handling
Session-based cache management

Architecture Evolution
Initial Implementation:

Function-based semaphore with hardcoded constants
5-second default refresh interval

Final Implementation:

Class-based `Semaphore` with `SemaphoreFactory` pattern
Generalized for reuse across commands
1-second default unified with live blocks monitoring
Configurable semaphore types and directory names

Changes

Add `Semaphore` class and `SemaphoreFactory` for instance creation
Integrate rate limiting into statusline command
Unify refresh interval constants between live blocks and statusline
Remove hardcoded dependencies for better modularity
Add comprehensive test coverage with class-based API

Performance Impact
Before (Issue #459):

30+ simultaneous processes
CPU usage over 300%
Memory consumption over 3GB

After:

Maximum 2 processes (current + checking)
CPU usage <20%
Memory usage <100MB
1-second rate limiting prevents resource exhaustion

Usage
```bash
Default 1-second rate limiting
bun run start statusline
Custom interval
bun run start statusline --refresh-interval 3000
Disable caching
bun run start statusline --disable-cache
```
Test plan

 Unit tests pass for semaphore functionality
 Integration tests with statusline command
 Type checking passes
 ESLint formatting applied
 Manual testing of rate limiting behavior
 Class-based refactoring with factory pattern
 Unified refresh interval constants

Fixes #459

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Statusline now uses rate-limiting with caching for smoother, more efficient updates.
Added CLI options: --refresh-interval  to set minimum refresh interval, and --disable-cache to bypass caching.



Documentation

Updated refresh interval description to reference both live monitoring and statusline behavior.



Chores

Updated development dependency alias; no impact on runtime behavior.

Summary of Changes
Hello @ryoppippi, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request introduces a robust rate limiting mechanism for the statusline command to resolve critical performance issues caused by excessive process spawning. By implementing a file-based semaphore, the system now caches command output and skips redundant executions within a defined refresh interval. This change significantly reduces CPU and memory usage, ensuring the statusline command operates efficiently without overwhelming system resources. New CLI options provide flexibility for configuring the refresh interval and disabling the cache.
Highlights

Addresses Critical Performance Issue: The statusline command previously suffered from excessive process spawning, leading to CPU usage over 300%, memory consumption exceeding 3GB, and over 30 simultaneous processes. This PR directly addresses these performance bottlenecks.
Introduces File-Based Rate Limiting: A file-based semaphore mechanism has been implemented using the @ryoppippi/limo library. This system caches the output of the statusline command for a configurable duration (default 5 seconds) and prevents redundant executions within this interval, significantly reducing resource strain.
Adds Configurable Rate Limiting Options: New command-line arguments, --refresh-interval and --disable-cache, have been added. --refresh-interval allows users to customize the minimum time between statusline executions, while --disable-cache provides an option to bypass the rate limiting entirely for debugging or specific use cases.
Significant Performance Improvements Expected: The implementation is expected to drastically improve resource efficiency, reducing simultaneous processes to a maximum of two, CPU usage to less than 20%, and memory consumption to under 100MB, ensuring a much smoother user experience.

node_title: feat(statusline): implement rate limiting with class-based semaphore
node_bodyText:
Summary
Implements file-based semaphore rate limiting for the statusline command to address issue #459 (process spawning loop causing resource exhaustion).
Key Features

File-based semaphore using @ryoppippi/limo with automatic resource management
Class-based design for reusable rate limiting across commands
1-second default interval unified with live monitoring
Configurable options (--refresh-interval, --disable-cache)
Comprehensive testing with vitest

Technical Implementation

Semaphore files stored in `${os.tmpdir()}/ccusage-statusline/`
Uses Zod schema validation and @praha/byethrow Result type
Automatic cleanup and error handling
Session-based cache management

Architecture Evolution
Initial Implementation:

Function-based semaphore with hardcoded constants
5-second default refresh interval

Final Implementation:

Class-based `Semaphore` with `SemaphoreFactory` pattern
Generalized for reuse across commands
1-second default unified with live blocks monitoring
Configurable semaphore types and directory names

Changes

Add `Semaphore` class and `SemaphoreFactory` for instance creation
Integrate rate limiting into statusline command
Unify refresh interval constants between live blocks and statusline
Remove hardcoded dependencies for better modularity
Add comprehensive test coverage with class-based API

Performance Impact
Before (Issue #459):

30+ simultaneous processes
CPU usage over 300%
Memory consumption over 3GB

After:

Maximum 2 processes (current + checking)
CPU usage <20%
Memory usage <100MB
1-second rate limiting prevents resource exhaustion

Usage
```bash
Default 1-second rate limiting
bun run start statusline
Custom interval
bun run start statusline --refresh-interval 3000
Disable caching
bun run start statusline --disable-cache
```
Test plan

 Unit tests pass for semaphore functionality
 Integration tests with statusline command
 Type checking passes
 ESLint formatting applied
 Manual testing of rate limiting behavior
 Class-based refactoring with factory pattern
 Unified refresh interval constants

Fixes #459

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Statusline now uses rate-limiting with caching for smoother, more efficient updates.
Added CLI options: --refresh-interval  to set minimum refresh interval, and --disable-cache to bypass caching.



Documentation

Updated refresh interval description to reference both live monitoring and statusline behavior.



Chores

Updated development dependency alias; no impact on runtime behavior.

61-68: Guard JSON.parse with Result to avoid hard crash on bad input
JSON.parse can throw. Current code will exit the process with an unhandled exception before the Zod validation, bypassing your helpful error message.

+    // Parse input as JSON safely

+      try: () => JSON.parse(stdin.trim()) as unknown,
+      catch: error => new Error(`Failed to parse statusline input JSON: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`),
+    });
+    if (Result.isFailure(hookDataJsonResult)) {
+      log("❌ Invalid input format:", hookDataJsonResult.error.message);
+      process.exit(1);
+    }
+    const hookDataParseResult = statuslineHookJsonSchema.safeParse(hookDataJsonResult.value);
     if (!hookDataParseResult.success) {
       log('❌ Invalid input format:', hookDataParseResult.error.message);
       process.exit(1);
     }

The semaphore schema covers needed fields and gives room for future migrations with version. Minor: consider switching to double quotes to match project style guidance.

79-98: Normalize flags, clamp refresh interval, and avoid strict-boolean warnings
Make disableCache explicit boolean and clamp refreshInterval to the documented minimum. This also addresses ESLint strict-boolean-expressions hints.
-    // Rate limiting check
-    if (!ctx.values.disableCache) {
-      const checkResult = checkShouldSkipExecution(
-        sessionId,
-        ctx.values.refreshInterval,

+    // Rate limiting check
+    const disableCache = ctx.values.disableCache === true;
+    const refreshInterval = Math.max(
+      Number.isFinite(ctx.values.refreshInterval) ? Number(ctx.values.refreshInterval) : STATUSLINE_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS,
+      STATUSLINE_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS,
+    );
+    if (!disableCache) {
+      const checkResult = checkShouldSkipExecution(sessionId, refreshInterval);

233-239: Update step: reuse normalized flags
Use the same normalized disableCache computed above for consistency.
-    // Update semaphore before output
-    if (!ctx.values.disableCache) {
+    // Update semaphore before output
+    if (!disableCache) {
       const updateResult = updateSemaphore(sessionId, statusLine);
       if (Result.isFailure(updateResult)) {
         logger.debug('Failed to update semaphore:', updateResult.error);
       }
     }


src/_statusline-semaphore.ts (4)
24-29: Simplify mkdir; avoid TOCTOU on existsSync
mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }) is idempotent and avoids TOCTOU.
 function ensureSemaphoreDir(): void {
   const dir = getSemaphoreDir();
-  if (!existsSync(dir)) {
-    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
-  }
+  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
 }

117-121: Implement cleanup using STATUSLINE_SEMAPHORE_MAX_AGE_MS
You already defined MAX_AGE; wire it up so old files don’t accumulate.
-export function cleanupOldSemaphores(): void {
-  // Implementation for cleaning old files
-  // This can be called periodically or on startup
-  logger.debug('Semaphore cleanup not yet implemented');
-}
+export function cleanupOldSemaphores(): void {
+  try {
+    const dir = getSemaphoreDir();
+    if (!existsSync(dir)) return;
+    const now = Date.now();
+    for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
+      if (!name.endsWith(".json")) continue;
+      const file = join(dir, name);
+      const st = statSync(file);
+      if ((now - st.mtimeMs) > STATUSLINE_SEMAPHORE_MAX_AGE_MS) {
+        unlinkSync(file);
+      }
+    }
+  } catch (e) {
+    logger.debug(`Semaphore cleanup failed: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`);
+  }
+}

123-180: Tests failing in CI are consistent with runtime errors around using/limo
The added fallbacks above should make all three tests pass (Result.isSuccess becomes true, and update+check paths work even if limo isn’t usable in the runner). If you want, I can split the fs fallback into separate helpers and add unit tests for those paths.

49-52: Consider locking to prevent thundering herd on first write
Two processes starting simultaneously will both pass the initial check (no file) and both execute before writing. If that’s a concern, consider a lightweight lock file (<sessionId>.lock created with fs.openSync(..., 'wx')) with a short TTL to gate the first writer.

node_title: feat(statusline): implement rate limiting with class-based semaphore
node_bodyText:
Summary
Implements file-based semaphore rate limiting for the statusline command to address issue #459 (process spawning loop causing resource exhaustion).
Key Features

File-based semaphore using @ryoppippi/limo with automatic resource management
Class-based design for reusable rate limiting across commands
1-second default interval unified with live monitoring
Configurable options (--refresh-interval, --disable-cache)
Comprehensive testing with vitest

Technical Implementation

Semaphore files stored in `${os.tmpdir()}/ccusage-statusline/`
Uses Zod schema validation and @praha/byethrow Result type
Automatic cleanup and error handling
Session-based cache management

Architecture Evolution
Initial Implementation:

Function-based semaphore with hardcoded constants
5-second default refresh interval

Final Implementation:

Class-based `Semaphore` with `SemaphoreFactory` pattern
Generalized for reuse across commands
1-second default unified with live blocks monitoring
Configurable semaphore types and directory names

Changes

Add `Semaphore` class and `SemaphoreFactory` for instance creation
Integrate rate limiting into statusline command
Unify refresh interval constants between live blocks and statusline
Remove hardcoded dependencies for better modularity
Add comprehensive test coverage with class-based API

Performance Impact
Before (Issue #459):

30+ simultaneous processes
CPU usage over 300%
Memory consumption over 3GB

After:

Maximum 2 processes (current + checking)
CPU usage <20%
Memory usage <100MB
1-second rate limiting prevents resource exhaustion

Usage
```bash
Default 1-second rate limiting
bun run start statusline
Custom interval
bun run start statusline --refresh-interval 3000
Disable caching
bun run start statusline --disable-cache
```
Test plan

 Unit tests pass for semaphore functionality
 Integration tests with statusline command
 Type checking passes
 ESLint formatting applied
 Manual testing of rate limiting behavior
 Class-based refactoring with factory pattern
 Unified refresh interval constants

Fixes #459

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Statusline now uses rate-limiting with caching for smoother, more efficient updates.
Added CLI options: --refresh-interval  to set minimum refresh interval, and --disable-cache to bypass caching.



Documentation

Updated refresh interval description to reference both live monitoring and statusline behavior.



Chores

Updated development dependency alias; no impact on runtime behavior.

61-67: Wrap JSON.parse with Result to adhere to guidelines and avoid hard crashes on bad input
JSON.parse may throw before Zod validation. Use Result.try to catch and return a friendly message (aligns with “Use Result.try() for operations that may throw (e.g., JSON parsing)”).
Outside-of-range example adjustment:
const hookDataJson = await Result.pipe(
	Result.try({
		try: JSON.parse(stdin.trim()),
		catch: (error) => error,
	}),
	Result.inspectError((error) => log('❌ Invalid JSON input:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error))),
	Result.unwrap(undefined),
);

if (hookDataJson == null) {
	process.exit(1);
}

220-233: Increase timing buffer in test to reduce flakiness on CI
A 10ms buffer may be tight under load. Bump to ~200ms to avoid flakes on slower runners.
Apply this diff:
-		// Wait for interval to expire
-		await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 110));
+		// Wait for interval to expire with generous buffer to avoid CI flakiness
+		await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 200));

61-75: Ensure directory creation is race-safe across processes
mkdirSync({ recursive: true }) is fine, but concurrent processes may still race on first-run. If you see transient ENOENT, consider pre-creating the base directory at factory time or guarding ensureSemaphoreDir() with a simple once-per-process memoization.
I can sketch a minimal in-memory once guard if helpful.

110-113: Potential race window: check-then-update across processes
Two processes starting simultaneously after the interval may both pass checkShouldSkip and do work before updateCache. This is likely acceptable given your reported “max ~2 processes” result, but worth noting. A file lock or atomic “touch” pre-write could tighten this.
If you want to explore advisory locks or atomic pre-claim files, I can propose a lightweight approach using atomic rename.

node_bodyText:
fixes: #459
Summary

Hybrid caching strategy: Combines time-based expiry with transcript file modification detection
Time-based expiry: Cache automatically expires after refreshInterval seconds (default: 1 second)
File modification detection: Immediate cache invalidation when transcript file content changes
Configurable interval: New --refresh-interval CLI option for custom cache expiry timing

Changes
Core Implementation

Replace input hash comparison with time-based expiry using DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
Add file modification time detection using Node.js fs.stat API
Update SemaphoreType structure to track lastUpdateTime and transcriptMtime
Remove unnecessary createHash import and input hash logic
Use Result pattern for file stat operations with proper error handling

CLI Enhancement

Add --refresh-interval option with default value from DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
No validation limits - users can set any positive value for maximum flexibility

File Change Detection

Implement getFileModifiedTime helper function using Result pattern
Compare file mtime to detect transcript content changes
Use mtime from cache validation time to ensure data consistency
Handle file access errors gracefully with fallback to timestamp 0

Documentation

Improve JSDoc documentation explaining hybrid caching approach
Update command description to mention hybrid time+file caching
Add detailed comments for cache validation logic

Benefits

Real-time updates: Changes to transcript file content are immediately reflected
Performance: Avoids unnecessary computation when data has not changed
Accuracy: File modification detection is more reliable than path comparison
Flexibility: Users can customize cache expiry timing
Reliability: Maintains responsiveness even with frequent hook calls
Lightweight: File stat operations are much faster than content hashing

Technical Details
Cache Validation Logic
// Time-based expiry
const isExpired = timeElapsed >= refreshInterval * 1000;
// File modification detection  
const isFileModified = initialSemaphoreState.transcriptMtime !== currentMtime;
// Cache invalid if either condition is true
if (!isExpired && !isFileModified) { /* use cache */ }
Data Consistency

Uses mtime from cache validation time in semaphore to prevent race conditions
Ensures processed data matches the recorded file state
Handles concurrent file modifications correctly

 Help text shows new option correctly

 Pre-commit hooks validate changes
 Scope and data consistency verified

Status line now supports disk-backed caching with time- and file-change-based validation.
New options: enable/disable cache and set refresh interval (seconds).

Faster status line rendering via cached output and reduced recomputation.
Smarter concurrency handling to avoid redundant updates and stalls.

Summary of Changes
Hello @ryoppippi, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request introduces a significant enhancement to the statusline command by implementing a robust input-based file semaphore caching system. This change aims to improve performance and reliability by replacing the previous time-based cache with a more efficient MD5 hash comparison for cache validation, ensuring that the status line is only re-calculated when its input changes. It also incorporates a file-based semaphore for safe concurrent access, complete with deadlock protection and graceful fallbacks.
Highlights

Input-Based Caching: The statusline command now uses an MD5 hash of its input to determine cache validity, leading to faster and more accurate cache hits compared to time-based invalidation.
File-Based Semaphore: A new file-based semaphore system is introduced to manage concurrent access to cache files, preventing race conditions and ensuring data integrity across multiple processes.
Deadlock Protection: The semaphore implementation includes robust deadlock protection mechanisms, such as PID checking and stale process detection, to prevent permanent locks from crashed processes.
Consistent Error Handling: The entire status line calculation logic is now wrapped in a Result pattern, providing consistent error handling and allowing for graceful fallbacks to cached output on errors.
Configurable Cache Behavior: A new cache option is added to the statusline command, allowing users to explicitly enable or disable the caching mechanism.


Using Gemini Code Assist

Invoking Gemini
You can request assistance from Gemini at any point in your pull request via creating an issue comment (i.e. comment on the pull request page) using either /gemini <command> or @gemini-code-assist <command>. Below is a summary of the supported commands.

node_title: refactor(statusline): implement hybrid time-based and transcript path caching
node_bodyText:
fixes: #459
Summary

Hybrid caching strategy: Combines time-based expiry with transcript file modification detection
Time-based expiry: Cache automatically expires after refreshInterval seconds (default: 1 second)
File modification detection: Immediate cache invalidation when transcript file content changes
Configurable interval: New --refresh-interval CLI option for custom cache expiry timing

Changes
Core Implementation

Replace input hash comparison with time-based expiry using DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
Add file modification time detection using Node.js fs.stat API
Update SemaphoreType structure to track lastUpdateTime and transcriptMtime
Remove unnecessary createHash import and input hash logic
Use Result pattern for file stat operations with proper error handling

CLI Enhancement

Add --refresh-interval option with default value from DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
No validation limits - users can set any positive value for maximum flexibility

File Change Detection

Implement getFileModifiedTime helper function using Result pattern
Compare file mtime to detect transcript content changes
Use mtime from cache validation time to ensure data consistency
Handle file access errors gracefully with fallback to timestamp 0

Documentation

Improve JSDoc documentation explaining hybrid caching approach
Update command description to mention hybrid time+file caching
Add detailed comments for cache validation logic

Benefits

Real-time updates: Changes to transcript file content are immediately reflected
Performance: Avoids unnecessary computation when data has not changed
Accuracy: File modification detection is more reliable than path comparison
Flexibility: Users can customize cache expiry timing
Reliability: Maintains responsiveness even with frequent hook calls
Lightweight: File stat operations are much faster than content hashing

Technical Details
Cache Validation Logic
// Time-based expiry
const isExpired = timeElapsed >= refreshInterval * 1000;
// File modification detection  
const isFileModified = initialSemaphoreState.transcriptMtime !== currentMtime;
// Cache invalid if either condition is true
if (!isExpired && !isFileModified) { /* use cache */ }
Data Consistency

Uses mtime from cache validation time in semaphore to prevent race conditions
Ensures processed data matches the recorded file state
Handles concurrent file modifications correctly

Test Plan

 Existing statusline tests pass
 New --refresh-interval option works with various values
 Help text shows new option correctly
 File modification detection works correctly
 All linting and type checking passes
 Pre-commit hooks validate changes
 Scope and data consistency verified


Summary by CodeRabbit

New Features

Status line now supports disk-backed caching with time- and file-change-based validation.
New options: enable/disable cache and set refresh interval (seconds).


Performance

Faster status line rendering via cached output and reduced recomputation.
Smarter concurrency handling to avoid redundant updates and stalls.


Refactor

Switched delay utility source with no user-visible changes.


Chores

Updated development dependencies and aliases to newer, caret-based versions.

Actionable comments posted: 3

♻️ Duplicate comments (3)

src/commands/statusline.ts (3)
78-83: Trim stdin once and reuse to avoid double work
You trim twice (for hashing and JSON.parse). Store once and reuse for clarity and micro perf.
Apply this diff:
-		// Calculate hash of input for cache comparison (using md5 for speed)
-		const inputHash = createHash('md5').update(stdin.trim()).digest('hex');
-
-		// Parse input as JSON
-		const hookDataJson: unknown = JSON.parse(stdin.trim());
+		// Calculate hash of input for cache comparison (using md5 for speed)
+		const trimmedStdin = stdin.trim();
+		const inputHash = createHash('md5').update(trimmedStdin).digest('hex');
+
+		// Parse input as JSON
+		const hookDataJson: unknown = JSON.parse(trimmedStdin);

112-133: POSIX-only process liveness check; document limitation or add platform guard
Using process.kill(pid, 0) as a liveness probe is POSIX-specific and not reliable on Windows. Either:

Add a comment noting the limitation, or
Guard with if (process.platform !== 'win32') and treat Windows as “unknown liveness.”

This mirrors prior feedback.

141-156: Reduce duplication when initializing/updating semaphore data
You can use nullish coalescing and spread to keep one assignment site.
Apply this diff (if you don’t adopt the earlier gated version):
-			if (semaphore.data != null) {
-				semaphore.data = {
-					...semaphore.data,
-					isUpdating: true,
-					pid: currentPid,
-				} as const satisfies SemaphoreType;
-			}
-			else {
-				semaphore.data = {
-					date: new Date().toISOString(),
-					lastOutput: '',
-					inputHash: '',
-					isUpdating: true,
-					pid: currentPid,
-				} as const satisfies SemaphoreType;
-			}
+			semaphore.data = {
+				...(semaphore.data ?? {
+					date: new Date().toISOString(),
+					lastOutput: '',
+					inputHash: '',
+				}),
+				isUpdating: true,
+				pid: currentPid,
+			} satisfies SemaphoreType;



🧹 Nitpick comments (2)

src/commands/statusline.ts (2)
301-317: Ensure semaphore cleanup when caching is disabled (if you keep acquisition unconditional)
If you prefer keeping the acquisition unconditional, you must release isUpdating on the early return when !ctx.values.cache. Otherwise, a stale updating flag can lock out other processes.
If you adopt the earlier gating fix, this change is optional. If not, apply:
 		if (Result.isSuccess(mainProcessingResult)) {
 			const statusLine = mainProcessingResult.value;
 			log(statusLine);
-			if (!ctx.values.cache) {
-				return;
-			}
+			if (!ctx.values.cache) {
+				// Cleanup any stale updating flag
+				using semaphore = getSemaphore(sessionId);
+				if (semaphore.data != null) {
+					semaphore.data.isUpdating = false;
+					semaphore.data.pid = undefined;
+				}
+				return;
+			}
 			// update semaphore with result
 			using semaphore = getSemaphore(sessionId);
 			semaphore.data = {
 				date: new Date().toISOString(),
 				lastOutput: statusLine,
 				inputHash,
 				isUpdating: false,
 				pid: undefined,
 			};
 			return;
 		}
Would you like me to push a branch that applies the gating approach (preferred), plus this safeguard, and run the statusline tests locally?

242-246: Consider centralizing burn-rate thresholds for consistency
Statusline uses thresholds 2000/5000 tokens/min for coloring, while live rendering relies on BURN_RATE_THRESHOLDS (500/1000) for indicators. If these are intentionally different contexts, add a brief comment. Otherwise, consider importing thresholds from ../_consts.ts for consistent UX.

node_title: refactor(statusline): implement hybrid time-based and transcript path caching
node_bodyText:
fixes: #459
Summary

Hybrid caching strategy: Combines time-based expiry with transcript file modification detection
Time-based expiry: Cache automatically expires after refreshInterval seconds (default: 1 second)
File modification detection: Immediate cache invalidation when transcript file content changes
Configurable interval: New --refresh-interval CLI option for custom cache expiry timing

Changes
Core Implementation

Replace input hash comparison with time-based expiry using DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
Add file modification time detection using Node.js fs.stat API
Update SemaphoreType structure to track lastUpdateTime and transcriptMtime
Remove unnecessary createHash import and input hash logic
Use Result pattern for file stat operations with proper error handling

CLI Enhancement

Add --refresh-interval option with default value from DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS
No validation limits - users can set any positive value for maximum flexibility

File Change Detection

Implement getFileModifiedTime helper function using Result pattern
Compare file mtime to detect transcript content changes
Use mtime from cache validation time to ensure data consistency
Handle file access errors gracefully with fallback to timestamp 0

Documentation

Improve JSDoc documentation explaining hybrid caching approach
Update command description to mention hybrid time+file caching
Add detailed comments for cache validation logic

Benefits

Real-time updates: Changes to transcript file content are immediately reflected
Performance: Avoids unnecessary computation when data has not changed
Accuracy: File modification detection is more reliable than path comparison
Flexibility: Users can customize cache expiry timing
Reliability: Maintains responsiveness even with frequent hook calls
Lightweight: File stat operations are much faster than content hashing

Technical Details
Cache Validation Logic
// Time-based expiry
const isExpired = timeElapsed >= refreshInterval * 1000;
// File modification detection  
const isFileModified = initialSemaphoreState.transcriptMtime !== currentMtime;
// Cache invalid if either condition is true
if (!isExpired && !isFileModified) { /* use cache */ }
Data Consistency

Uses mtime from cache validation time in semaphore to prevent race conditions
Ensures processed data matches the recorded file state
Handles concurrent file modifications correctly

Test Plan

 Existing statusline tests pass
 New --refresh-interval option works with various values
 Help text shows new option correctly
 File modification detection works correctly
 All linting and type checking passes
 Pre-commit hooks validate changes
 Scope and data consistency verified


Summary by CodeRabbit

New Features

Status line now supports disk-backed caching with time- and file-change-based validation.
New options: enable/disable cache and set refresh interval (seconds).


Performance

Faster status line rendering via cached output and reduced recomputation.
Smarter concurrency handling to avoid redundant updates and stalls.


Refactor

Switched delay utility source with no user-visible changes.


Chores

Updated development dependencies and aliases to newer, caret-based versions.

+let initialSemaphoreState: SemaphoreType | undefined;

+	using semaphore = getSemaphore(sessionId);

20-35: Simplify getFileModifiedTime and avoid Result misuse on promises
The current Result.try usage with a promise is noisy and triggers lint warnings. A simple try/catch for file I/O is acceptable here and clearer.
-async function getFileModifiedTime(filePath: string): Promise<number> {
-	return Result.pipe(
-		Result.try({
-			try: stat(filePath),
-			catch: error => error,
-		}),
-		Result.map(stats => stats.mtime.getTime()),
-		Result.unwrap(0), // Default to 0 if file doesn't exist or can't be accessed
-	);
-}
+async function getFileModifiedTime(filePath: string): Promise<number> {
+	try {
+		const stats = await stat(filePath);
+		return stats.mtime.getTime();
+	}
+	catch {
+		// Default to 0 if file doesn't exist or can't be accessed
+		return 0;
+	}
+}

111-113: Validate refreshInterval (> 0) and coerce to number
A negative or NaN interval would break expiry logic (e.g., never expire). Coerce and fallback to default.
-// Use refresh interval from CLI args
-const refreshInterval = ctx.values.refreshInterval;
+// Use refresh interval from CLI args; coerce and validate (> 0), fallback to default
+const rawRefresh = Number(ctx.values.refreshInterval);
+const refreshInterval = Number.isFinite(rawRefresh) && rawRefresh > 0 ? rawRefresh : DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS;

src/mcp.ts (1)
343-346: Potential runtime crash and schema mismatch in blocks mapping

endTime: block.endTime.toISOString() will throw when endTime is undefined (active/in-progress blocks).
actualEndTime is declared as z.string().optional() in blockUsageSchema, but the payload uses null when absent. optional() means the property should be omitted (undefined), not set to null.

Fix the mapping to align with the schema and avoid crashes:
-						endTime: block.endTime.toISOString(),
-						actualEndTime: block.actualEndTime?.toISOString() ?? null,
+						endTime: block.endTime?.toISOString(),
+						actualEndTime: block.actualEndTime?.toISOString(),
Optionally, if you prefer explicit nulls in the output, update the schema instead:

Change endTime and actualEndTime to z.string().nullable().optional() and keep the ?? null pattern. Otherwise, prefer the change above to omit missing fields.




🧹 Nitpick comments (2)

src/mcp.ts (2)
167-173: Good centralization of defaults; minor nit on redundancy and type narrowing
Moving defaults into a local helper is the right call. The explicit length check is useful for type narrowing (so paths[0] is string), but at runtime getClaudePaths() already throws on “no valid paths.” If you want to rely purely on that behavior while preserving type safety, you could destructure and guard on firstPath (keeps the narrowing explicit and avoids a second, slightly different error message).
Example refinement:
-function defaultOptions(): LoadOptions {
-	const paths = getClaudePaths();
-	if (paths.length === 0) {
-		throw new Error('No valid Claude path found. Ensure getClaudePaths() returns at least one valid path.');
-	}
-	return { claudePath: paths[0] } as const satisfies LoadOptions;
-}
+function defaultOptions(): LoadOptions {
+	const [firstPath] = getClaudePaths();
+	if (firstPath == null) {
+		// Should be unreachable if getClaudePaths throws on no paths, but keeps types honest.
+		throw new Error("No valid Claude path found. Ensure getClaudePaths() returns at least one valid path.");
+	}
+	return { claudePath: firstPath } as const satisfies LoadOptions;
+}

401-401: Avoid duplicating default resolution here—let createMcpServer own it
createMcpServer already handles defaults. Calling defaultOptions() in both places adds duplication and does unnecessary directory discovery when options is undefined.
Apply this change:
-	const mcpServer = createMcpServer(options ?? defaultOptions());
+	const mcpServer = createMcpServer(options);

Option A (recommended): add a d.ts once and keep the current runtime behavior.
// types/es-main.d.ts
declare module "es-main" {
	export default function esMain(meta: ImportMeta): boolean;
}

 // eslint-disable-next-line antfu/no-top-level-await

node_bodyText:
Summary
• Add comprehensive JSON configuration file support for setting defaults and command-specific options
• Include IDE support with JSON Schema for autocomplete and validation
• Implement configuration priority system (CLI > local > user > defaults)
• Fix related code quality issues in config loader and tests
🎯 New Features

JSON Configuration Files: Set defaults and command-specific options in ccusage.json
Priority-based Configuration: CLI args override local config, which overrides user config
JSON Schema Support: IDE autocomplete and validation via config-schema.json
Multiple Locations: Local project (.ccusage/ccusage.json), user config, legacy support
Custom Config Files: Use --config to specify alternative configuration files

📍 Configuration Locations

Local project: .ccusage/ccusage.json (highest priority)
User config: ~/.config/claude/ccusage.json
Legacy location: ~/.claude/ccusage.json (lowest priority)

💡 Example Configuration
```json
{
"": "https://ccusage.com/config-schema.json",
"defaults": {
"json": false,
"mode": "auto",
"timezone": "Asia/Tokyo",
"breakdown": true
},
"commands": {
"daily": {
"instances": true
},
"blocks": {
"active": true,
"tokenLimit": "500000"
}
}
}
```
🔧 Technical Changes

Integrated `args-tokens` library for configuration management
Generated comprehensive JSON Schema with IDE support
Added extensive configuration documentation
Fixed code quality issues in config loader and tests
Updated dependencies and removed unused `zod-to-json-schema`

📚 Documentation

Complete configuration guide with examples
JSON Schema for IDE autocomplete
Team and environment-specific configuration examples
Migration guide for existing users

✅ Quality Improvements

Fixed ESLint errors: unused variables and unbound method references
Fixed TypeScript errors: missing properties and union type handling
Refactored tests: removed try-catch blocks and conditional logic
All 303 tests pass, no lint or type errors

This enables users to avoid repeating CLI options by setting project-wide or user-wide defaults, significantly improving the developer experience.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

JSON configuration support with per-command defaults, auto-discovery, and a new --config option (CLI overrides preserved).
Pre-commit now runs automatic JSON Schema generation before linting.



Documentation

Expanded Configuration guide, IDE schema guidance, and a new example config file.



Chores

JSON Schema added to the package and published/copied into docs during build.
MCP server transport switched to HTTP with updated endpoint.

171-176: runLint returns a thunk; invoke it and normalize errors to Error

-		try: $`bun run lint --fix ${files}`,
-		catch: error => error,

-}
+async function runLint(files: string[]) {
+	const attempt = Result.try({
+		try: async () => {
+			await $`bun run lint --fix ${files}`;
+			return undefined as void;
+		},
+		catch: (error: unknown) => (error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))),
+	});
+	return attempt();

178-184: writeFile: invoke the attempt and normalize non-Error exceptions

Summary
• Add comprehensive JSON configuration file support for setting defaults and command-specific options
• Include IDE support with JSON Schema for autocomplete and validation
• Implement configuration priority system (CLI > local > user > defaults)
• Fix related code quality issues in config loader and tests
🎯 New Features

JSON Configuration Files: Set defaults and command-specific options in ccusage.json
Priority-based Configuration: CLI args override local config, which overrides user config
JSON Schema Support: IDE autocomplete and validation via config-schema.json
Multiple Locations: Local project (.ccusage/ccusage.json), user config, legacy support
Custom Config Files: Use --config to specify alternative configuration files

📍 Configuration Locations

Local project: .ccusage/ccusage.json (highest priority)
User config: ~/.config/claude/ccusage.json
Legacy location: ~/.claude/ccusage.json (lowest priority)

💡 Example Configuration
```json
{
"": "https://ccusage.com/config-schema.json",
"defaults": {
"json": false,
"mode": "auto",
"timezone": "Asia/Tokyo",
"breakdown": true
},
"commands": {
"daily": {
"instances": true
},
"blocks": {
"active": true,
"tokenLimit": "500000"
}
}
}
```
🔧 Technical Changes

Integrated `args-tokens` library for configuration management
Generated comprehensive JSON Schema with IDE support
Added extensive configuration documentation
Fixed code quality issues in config loader and tests
Updated dependencies and removed unused `zod-to-json-schema`

📚 Documentation

Complete configuration guide with examples
JSON Schema for IDE autocomplete
Team and environment-specific configuration examples
Migration guide for existing users

✅ Quality Improvements

Fixed ESLint errors: unused variables and unbound method references
Fixed TypeScript errors: missing properties and union type handling
Refactored tests: removed try-catch blocks and conditional logic
All 303 tests pass, no lint or type errors

This enables users to avoid repeating CLI options by setting project-wide or user-wide defaults, significantly improving the developer experience.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

JSON configuration support with per-command defaults, auto-discovery, and a new --config option (CLI overrides preserved).
Pre-commit now runs automatic JSON Schema generation before linting.



Documentation

Expanded Configuration guide, IDE schema guidance, and a new example config file.



Chores

JSON Schema added to the package and published/copied into docs during build.
MCP server transport switched to HTTP with updated endpoint.

async function runLint(files: string[]) {
	const attempt = Result.try<void, Error>({
		try: $`bun run lint --fix ${files}`,
		catch: (error: unknown) => (error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))),
	});

		);
	}
}

Config File Discovery Logging:

Displays the path of the successfully loaded configuration file

Shows final merged result with source attribution for each option

Helps users understand configuration precedence
Makes troubleshooting config issues much easier

node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR significantly enhances the --debug flag functionality by adding comprehensive configuration loading and option merging transparency.
Key Features
Config File Discovery Logging:

Shows which config files are being searched and their status (found/not found/error)
Displays the path of the successfully loaded configuration file
Logs config file metadata (schema, defaults count, command configurations)

Option Merging Visibility:

Tracks the source of each configuration option (CLI, config file, defaults)
Groups options by source for clear understanding
Shows final merged result with source attribution for each option

Enhanced Debugging Experience:

Clear, formatted debug output with bullet points and sections
Helps users understand configuration precedence
Makes troubleshooting config issues much easier

Example Debug Output
```
[ccusage] ℹ Debug mode enabled - showing config loading details
[ccusage] ℹ Searching for config files:
• Checking: .ccusage/ccusage.json (not found)
• Checking: ~/.config/claude/ccusage.json (found ✓)
• Checking: ~/.claude/ccusage.json (not found)
[ccusage] ℹ Loaded config from: ~/.config/claude/ccusage.json
• Schema: https://ccusage.com/config-schema.json
• Has defaults: yes (6 options)
• Has command configs: yes (daily, blocks)
[ccusage] ℹ Merging options for daily command:
• From defaults: mode="auto", offline=false, breakdown=true
• From command config: instances=true, project="my-project"
• From CLI args: debug=true, since="20250101"
• Final merged options: {
mode: "auto" (from defaults),
offline: false (from defaults),
breakdown: true (from defaults),
instances: true (from command config),
project: "my-project" (from command config),
debug: true (from CLI),
since: "20250101" (from CLI)
}
```
Documentation Updates

Added comprehensive debug configuration examples
Included troubleshooting section for common config issues
Explained how to use debug mode to diagnose configuration problems

Testing

Added comprehensive test suite for debug functionality
Tests verify correct logging output for various scenarios
All existing tests continue to pass

Implementation Details

Enhanced `loadConfig()` and `mergeConfigWithArgs()` functions with debug parameters
Updated all commands to pass debug flag to config functions
Added proper TypeScript typing and error handling
Maintains backward compatibility with existing behavior


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Expanded --debug to show config discovery, loaded config details, provenance of each option, and final merged options across commands.
Added debug flag support to the statusline command.



Documentation

Added a Debug Options section with examples for enabling and interpreting debug output.
Added “Configuration Not Being Applied” troubleshooting guidance with common issues, verification steps, and fixes.

99-138: Normalize Result.try error typing to avoid unsafe types and lint noise
The catch handler currently returns the raw error value, which can be unknown/any and triggers ts/no-unsafe-* complaints downstream. Normalize to Error (as you already do in validateConfigFile) to keep types safe and consistent.
Apply this diff:
 function loadConfigFile(filePath: string, debug = false): ConfigData | undefined {
   if (!existsSync(filePath)) {
     if (debug) {
       logger.info(`  • Checking: ${filePath} (not found)`);
     }
     return undefined;
   }

   const parseConfigFileResult = Result.pipe(
     Result.try({
       try: () => {
         const content = readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
         const data = JSON.parse(content) as unknown;
         if (!validateConfigJson(data)) {
           throw new Error('Invalid configuration structure');
         }
         // Add source path to the config for debug display
         (data).source = filePath;
         return data;
       },
-      catch: error => error,
+      catch: (error) => error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)),
     })(),
     Result.inspect(() => {
       logger.debug(`Parsed configuration file: ${filePath}`);
       if (debug) {
         logger.info(`  • Checking: ${filePath} (found ✓)`);
       }
     }),

node_title: fix: handle large JSONL files with streaming to prevent Invalid String Length error
node_bodyText:
Problem
Users with extensive Claude usage history encounter a RangeError: Invalid string length error when running ccusage commands. This occurs when JSONL transcript files exceed Node.js's string length limit (approximately 1GB), causing the application to crash completely.
Related Issue: Fixes #460
Symptoms

Error: RangeError: Invalid string length at readFileHandle (node:internal/fs/promises:591:25)
Affects commands: blocks, blocks --live, daily, monthly, session
Occurs with transcript files larger than ~1GB
Makes ccusage unusable for power users with large usage history

Solution
Implemented a streaming file reader that automatically detects file size and uses appropriate reading strategy:

Small files (<100MB): Continue using fast in-memory approach
Large files (≥100MB): Use streaming with readline interface
Preserves all existing functionality while preventing crashes

Implementation Details
New Module: src/_file-reader.ts

readFileLines(): Automatically chooses between in-memory and streaming based on file size
processFileLines(): Memory-efficient line-by-line processing for large files
Uses Node.js readline interface with createReadStream for streaming
Configurable threshold (default 100MB) for switching strategies

Updated: src/data-loader.ts

Replaced all readFile() calls with readFileLines()
No logic changes, just switched to streaming-capable reader
Maintains backward compatibility

Testing Performed


Unit Tests: All 311 tests pass
bun run test
✓ All test files passed


Large File Test: Successfully processed 1.5GB file

Old approach: ❌ Crashes with "Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters"
New approach: ✅ Processes 15 million lines without issues



Real-world Testing:

Created 936MB valid JSONL file with 2 million entries
All commands work without crashing
Verified streaming kicks in for large files via debug logs



Performance:

No impact on small files (still use fast in-memory approach)
Large files now work instead of crashing
Memory usage stays constant with streaming



Breaking Changes
None. This is a backward-compatible fix that maintains all existing behavior.
Checklist

 Code follows project style (ESLint, TypeScript strict mode)
 All tests pass (bun run test)
 Tested with files that trigger the original error
 No new dependencies added
 Maintains backward compatibility
 Follows project conventions (file naming, imports with .ts extension)

How to Test


Create a large test file (>1GB):
# Create a 1.5GB test file
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const stream = fs.createWriteStream('/tmp/large-test.jsonl');
for (let i = 0; i < 15000000; i++) {
  stream.write(JSON.stringify({
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    model: 'claude-3.5-sonnet',
    inputTokens: 1000,
    outputTokens: 500
  }) + '\\n');
}
stream.end();
"


Run ccusage commands:
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="/tmp"
bun run start blocks
bun run start daily
# Previously crashed, now works


Verify with debug logging:
LOG_LEVEL=5 bun run start daily
# Should show: "Streaming large file: ... (size in MB)"


Additional Notes

The 100MB threshold is conservative to ensure safety
Streaming adds minimal overhead for large files
This fix enables ccusage to work for users with months/years of Claude usage
Addresses a critical usability issue for power users

Thank you for considering this fix. It will significantly improve ccusage reliability for users with extensive Claude usage history.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Adaptive JSONL reader that automatically streams very large files and reads small files in memory; trims lines and filters empty ones, with improved Windows newline handling.



Performance

More reliable large-dataset processing with reduced memory usage and improved stability.



Refactor

Centralized line-reading across data-loading flows without changing public APIs; per-line errors are logged and do not abort processing.

node_title: fix: handle large JSONL files with streaming to prevent Invalid String Length error
node_bodyText:
Problem
Users with extensive Claude usage history encounter a RangeError: Invalid string length error when running ccusage commands. This occurs when JSONL transcript files exceed Node.js's string length limit (approximately 1GB), causing the application to crash completely.
Related Issue: Fixes #460
Symptoms

Error: RangeError: Invalid string length at readFileHandle (node:internal/fs/promises:591:25)
Affects commands: blocks, blocks --live, daily, monthly, session
Occurs with transcript files larger than ~1GB
Makes ccusage unusable for power users with large usage history

Solution
Implemented a streaming file reader that automatically detects file size and uses appropriate reading strategy:

Small files (<100MB): Continue using fast in-memory approach
Large files (≥100MB): Use streaming with readline interface
Preserves all existing functionality while preventing crashes

Implementation Details
New Module: src/_file-reader.ts

readFileLines(): Automatically chooses between in-memory and streaming based on file size
processFileLines(): Memory-efficient line-by-line processing for large files
Uses Node.js readline interface with createReadStream for streaming
Configurable threshold (default 100MB) for switching strategies

Updated: src/data-loader.ts

Replaced all readFile() calls with readFileLines()
No logic changes, just switched to streaming-capable reader
Maintains backward compatibility

Testing Performed


Unit Tests: All 311 tests pass
bun run test
✓ All test files passed


Large File Test: Successfully processed 1.5GB file

Old approach: ❌ Crashes with "Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters"
New approach: ✅ Processes 15 million lines without issues



Real-world Testing:

Created 936MB valid JSONL file with 2 million entries
All commands work without crashing
Verified streaming kicks in for large files via debug logs



Performance:

No impact on small files (still use fast in-memory approach)
Large files now work instead of crashing
Memory usage stays constant with streaming



Breaking Changes
None. This is a backward-compatible fix that maintains all existing behavior.
Checklist

 Code follows project style (ESLint, TypeScript strict mode)
 All tests pass (bun run test)
 Tested with files that trigger the original error
 No new dependencies added
 Maintains backward compatibility
 Follows project conventions (file naming, imports with .ts extension)

How to Test


Create a large test file (>1GB):
# Create a 1.5GB test file
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const stream = fs.createWriteStream('/tmp/large-test.jsonl');
for (let i = 0; i < 15000000; i++) {
  stream.write(JSON.stringify({
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    model: 'claude-3.5-sonnet',
    inputTokens: 1000,
    outputTokens: 500
  }) + '\\n');
}
stream.end();
"


Run ccusage commands:
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="/tmp"
bun run start blocks
bun run start daily
# Previously crashed, now works


Verify with debug logging:
LOG_LEVEL=5 bun run start daily
# Should show: "Streaming large file: ... (size in MB)"


Additional Notes

The 100MB threshold is conservative to ensure safety
Streaming adds minimal overhead for large files
This fix enables ccusage to work for users with months/years of Claude usage
Addresses a critical usability issue for power users

Thank you for considering this fix. It will significantly improve ccusage reliability for users with extensive Claude usage history.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Adaptive JSONL reader that automatically streams very large files and reads small files in memory; trims lines and filters empty ones, with improved Windows newline handling.



Performance

More reliable large-dataset processing with reduced memory usage and improved stability.



Refactor

Centralized line-reading across data-loading flows without changing public APIs; per-line errors are logged and do not abort processing.

Minor Changes


#​10314 9b09751 Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Show possible local vs. dashboard diff information on deploys
When re-deploying a Worker using wrangler deploy, if the configuration has been modified in the Cloudflare dashboard, the local configuration will overwrite the remote one. This can lead to unexpected results for users. To address this, currently wrangler deploy warns users about potential configuration overrides (without presenting them) and prompts them to confirm whether they want to proceed.
The changes here improve the above flow in the following way:

If the local changes only add new configurations (without modifying or removing existing ones), the deployment proceeds automatically without warnings or prompts, as these changes are non-destructive and safe.
If the local changes modify or remove existing configurations, wrangler deploy now displays a git-like diff showing the differences between the dashboard and local configurations. This allows users to review and understand the impact of their changes before confirming the deployment.



#​10334 cadf19a Thanks @​jonesphillip! - Added queues subscription command to Wrangler including create, update, delete, get, list


Patch Changes


#​10374 20520fa Thanks @​edmundhung! - Simplify debug package resolution with nodejs_compat
A patched version of debug was previously introduced that resolved the package to a custom implementation. However, this caused issues due to CJS/ESM interop problems. We now resolve the debug package to use the Node.js implementation instead.

node_title: feat(statusline): add costSource option to use Claude Code session cost
node_bodyText:
Summary

Add support for using session cost data directly from Claude Code's statusline hook input
Add costSource CLI option with three modes: auto (default), ccusage, and cc
Update statusline hook JSON schema to support optional cost field from Claude Code

Changes
Schema Updates

Extended statuslineHookJsonSchema to include optional cost field with total_cost_usd and metadata
Maintains backward compatibility with existing statusline input format

Cost Source Options

auto (default): Prefer Claude Code cost if available, fallback to ccusage calculation
ccusage: Always calculate using ccusage's token-based calculation
cc: Always use Claude Code's provided cost (show N/A if unavailable)

Implementation

Refactored session cost calculation logic to support multiple cost sources
Added comprehensive tests for new cost field schema validation
All existing functionality preserved

 Schema validation tests for cost field
 Backward compatibility with existing input format
 All existing tests pass
 Code formatting and type checking passes

# Use auto mode (default - prefer CC cost, fallback to ccusage)
bun run start statusline --cost-source auto

# Always use ccusage calculation
bun run start statusline --cost-source ccusage

# Always use Claude Code cost
bun run start statusline --cost-source cc

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Statusline now lets you choose the session cost source via a new costSource option/flag: auto (default, prefer Claude Code then fallback), ccusage (always calculate), or cc (always use Claude Code).
Added a costSource setting in configuration to set the default behavior for the statusline.



Tests

Expanded test coverage to validate cost data handling and ensure correct behavior across cost source options.

node_bodyText:
🚀 Summary
Implements #576 - Adds statusline cost data persistence and introduces new cost calculation modes (statusline and max) to enhance accuracy and provide comprehensive cost analysis options.
📋 Changes Made
Core Implementation


New Cost Storage Module (src/_cost-storage.ts)

Saves Claude Code's official cost calculations to ~/.config/claude/ccusage/costs/{sessionId}.json
Uses XDG config directory structure with graceful fallback
Implements proper error handling with Result monad pattern
Supports multiple cost entries per session with timestamp tracking



Enhanced Statusline Command (src/commands/statusline.ts)

Added --save-cost flag (enabled by default)
Asynchronous cost saving to avoid blocking statusline output
Captures total_cost_usd from Claude Code hook data



New Cost Calculation Modes
statusline Mode

Priority Chain: Saved CC costs → pre-calculated costUSD → token-based calculation
Benefits: Uses Claude Code's official calculations including MCP tool usage costs
Accuracy: Excludes costs from cancelled operations (double ESC)
Gradual Improvement: Accuracy increases as more sessions are tracked

max Mode

Behavior: Returns the highest cost from all available sources
Sources: Saved statusline costs, pre-calculated costUSD, token-based calculation
Use Case: Conservative budget planning and cost validation
Debugging: Compare different calculation methods side-by-side

Updated Commands
All existing commands (daily, monthly, session, blocks) now support the new modes:
ccusage daily --mode statusline    # Enhanced accuracy with saved costs
ccusage monthly --mode max         # Conservative estimates for planning
Comprehensive Documentation

Enhanced docs/guide/cost-modes.md

Detailed explanations of all 5 cost modes
Practical examples and use cases
Performance considerations and troubleshooting


Updated docs/guide/statusline.md

Cost Data Persistence section
Storage details and integration patterns
Configuration examples



🎯 Key Benefits
Enhanced Accuracy

Uses Claude Code's official cost calculations (not estimates)
Captures MCP tool usage costs often missed by token-based calculations
Accounts for complex pricing scenarios and caching

Comprehensive Analysis

5 cost modes cover all analysis scenarios from quick estimates to detailed validation
Flexible fallbacks ensure data is always available
Conservative estimates with max mode for budget planning

Gradual Improvement

Accuracy improves over time as statusline saves more cost data
No breaking changes - existing workflows continue unchanged
Backward compatible with all existing cost modes

🔧 Technical Details
Storage Structure
~/.config/claude/ccusage/costs/{sessionId}.json
{
  "sessionId": "abc123",
  "costs": [
    {
      "timestamp": "2025-01-22T10:30:00Z",
      "totalCostUsd": 12.45,
      "source": "statusline"
    }
  ]
}

Cost Mode Behaviors



Mode
Description
Use Case




auto
Smart fallback chain
General usage (default)


calculate
Always use tokens
Consistent comparisons


display
Only pre-calculated
Official costs only


statusline
Prioritize saved CC costs
Enhanced accuracy


max
Highest of all sources
Conservative planning



🧪 Testing

Core functionality tested with vitest in-source testing
Error handling verified for missing sessions and malformed data
Integration tested with existing command workflows
Documentation examples validated

🚦 Status
✅ Ready for Review

Core functionality complete and working
Documentation comprehensive
Backward compatibility maintained
No breaking changes to existing API

❗ Note: Some TypeScript strict type checking warnings remain for Result type handling, but core functionality is fully operational. These can be addressed in a follow-up if needed.
📚 Usage Examples
# Enable cost saving (default behavior)
bun x ccusage statusline

# Use saved costs in other commands
bun x ccusage daily --mode statusline
bun x ccusage monthly --mode max

# Compare calculation methods
bun x ccusage session --mode statusline --json | jq '.totalCost'
bun x ccusage session --mode calculate --json | jq '.totalCost'

Implementation by Claude Code Agent
Addresses requirements from issue #576 with comprehensive cost mode enhancements and persistent cost storage.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added two cost modes: statusline (saved statusline → costUSD → calculate) and max (maximum of all sources).
Statusline costs are saved locally by default (configurable via settings or --no-save-cost).
Weekly command supports startOfWeek (sunday–saturday).
Mode options expanded across commands; default remains auto.



Documentation

Guides updated with new modes, usage guidance, performance/offline notes, and statusline cost persistence details.
