Actionable comments posted: 4 ♻️ Duplicate comments (3) src/_cost-storage.ts (1) 77-124: Guard against concurrent writers (lost updates) with a per-file lock Concurrent statusline processes can interleave read-modify-write and drop entries. Add a simple lock (e.g., proper-lockfile) around the entire save section so only one writer operates at a time per session file. This prevents lost cost entries. I can add proper-lockfile usage (acquire before load/append/write, finally release) or a simple advisory .lock file strategy—your call. src/commands/statusline.ts (1) 469-481: Fix lint and type issues; use non-blocking async IIFE and explicit boolean check Current .then() chain and truthy check trip strict-boolean and unsafe-call rules. Replace with an async IIFE, keep it fire-and-forget with void, and compare saveCost === true explicitly. - // Save Claude Code cost data if available and enabled - if (ctx.values.saveCost && hookData.cost?.total_cost_usd != null) { - // Save cost asynchronously to avoid blocking statusline output - saveCostData(sessionId, hookData.cost.total_cost_usd) - .then((result) => { - if (Result.isFailure(result)) { - logger.debug(`Failed to save cost data: ${result.error.message}`); - } - }) - .catch((error: unknown) => { - logger.debug(`Error saving cost data: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`); - }); - } + // Save Claude Code cost data if available and enabled (non-blocking) + if (ctx.values.saveCost === true && hookData.cost?.total_cost_usd != null) { + void (async () => { + const result = await saveCostData(sessionId, hookData.cost!.total_cost_usd); + if (Result.isFailure(result)) { + logger.debug(`Failed to save cost data: ${result.error.message}`); + } + })().catch((error: unknown) => { + logger.debug(`Error saving cost data: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`); + }); + } src/data-loader.ts (1) 779-805: “max” mode suffers the same multiplication; apply the same caching now and plan session-level fix As above, saved costs should be considered once per session, not per entry. Apply the caching guard in the interim. if (mode === 'max') { // Max mode: MAX(saved statusline costs, pre-calculated costUSD, token-based calculation) const costs: number[] = []; // Get saved statusline cost if (data.sessionId != null) { - const savedCost = await getSavedCost(data.sessionId); - if (savedCost != null) { - costs.push(savedCost); - } + const sid = data.sessionId; + let savedCost = savedCostCache.get(sid); + if (savedCost === undefined && !savedCostCache.has(sid)) { + savedCost = await Result.unwrap( + Result.try({ + try: () => getSavedCost(sid), + catch: (e: unknown) => { + logger.debug(`getSavedCost failed for ${sid}: ${String(e)}`); + return e as Error; + }, + })(), + undefined, + ); + savedCostCache.set(sid, savedCost); + } + if (savedCost != null) { + costs.push(savedCost); + } } Follow-up (recommended): move saved-cost logic to loadSessionData and daily/weekly/monthly aggregations. 🧹 Nitpick comments (4) src/_cost-storage.ts (2) 131-147: Differentiate ENOENT vs. malformed JSON; avoid clobbering corrupt files silently Right now, saveCostData will recreate the file on any load failure—including schema errors—overwriting possibly recoverable data. Consider: Treat ENOENT as “no data” (OK to create). For parse/validation errors, return a failure Result and don’t overwrite; log a clear message and optionally write a .bak before attempting repair. I can wire a small helper to classify errors (code === 'ENOENT') and propagate others. 1-8: Style: switch to double quotes to align with repo TypeScript guidelines Imports and string literals use single quotes here. The codebase guideline prefers double quotes for .ts files. Consider running ESLint/formatter or updating literals in this file. src/data-loader.ts (1) 36-37: Direct dependency on storage API is fine; consider memoizing saved costs to reduce I/O Import is correct. Later calls to getSavedCost happen per entry—add a small per-run cache to avoid repeated disk reads for the same session. I propose a tiny Map at module scope; see diffs below in the mode branches. docs/guide/statusline.md (1) 256-337: Add language to fenced code block for path snippet; minor grammar polish Markdownlint prefers a language. Use “text” for file paths; also ensure “Claude Code” spelling consistency. -``` +```text ~/.config/claude/ccusage/costs/{sessionId}.json

bodyText:
Actionable comments posted: 2

🧹 Nitpick comments (2)

src/commands/_blocks.live.ts (1)
116-122: Refine error handling for delayWithAbort in _blocks.live.ts
The current code swallows all errors via Result.unwrap(undefined), making it unclear which errors you intend to ignore. We should:

Tighten the Result.try typing to avoid any ts/no-unsafe warnings by specifying <void, Error>.
Explicitly ignore only AbortError (the known shutdown signal) in Result.inspectError, and log any other unexpected errors at debug level.
Drop the DOMException check (our tsconfig only includes "ESNext", not the DOM lib, so DOMException isn’t recognized by the compiler).

Apply this optional refactor:
-		await Result.pipe(
-			Result.try({
-				try: async () => delayWithAbort(config.refreshInterval, abortController.signal),
-				catch: () => new Error('DelayWithAbort failed'),
-			})(),
-			Result.unwrap(undefined),
-		);
+		await Result.pipe(
+			// Only swallow AbortError; surface/log other failures
+			Result.try<void, Error>({
+				try: async () => {
+					await delayWithAbort(config.refreshInterval, abortController.signal);

max
median
avg

--token-limit-sessions (defaults to 10) - calculates limits over the previous number of sessions

 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit median --token-limit-sessions 5

With max:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit max --token-limit-sessions 5

Views, warnings, and logging now reflect calculated limits and warn when no completed sessions exist.



Documentation

Guides expanded with methods, examples, migration notes, and live-monitoring guidance.



Tests

Added tests covering calculation methods and CLI scenarios.

577-1110: Clarification on parseTokenLimit behavior and test placement
Upon inspecting the parseTokenLimit helper, it only recognizes empty/undefined, "max", or explicit numeric strings—anything else (including "avg" or "median") is treated as invalid and yields undefined (or the default when empty) rather than delegating to the average/median logic handled elsewhere. Therefore:

Adding a test like
expect(parseTokenLimit('avg', 1234)).toBe(1234);
expect(parseTokenLimit('median', 4321)).toBe(4321);
would not reflect the real behavior of parseTokenLimit. Coverage for the "avg" and "median" methods belongs in the token-limit calculation routines (e.g., in tests around loadSessionBlockData or wherever you dispatch on tokenLimitMethod), not in parseTokenLimit.

That said, renaming
- it('uses default values correctly', () => {
+ it('uses mock-context defaults correctly', () => {
is still sensible to avoid confusion between test fixtures and actual CLI defaults.
Given this mismatch, you can safely ignore the proposed parseTokenLimit('avg'…) tests. Instead, ensure you have dedicated tests for each tokenLimitMethod in the calculation logic.

node_title: feat: adding configurable token limits
node_bodyText:
This PR fixes #145 and #483 by adding the ability for configurable token limits and calculation methods. This allows for much more accurate token limit estimations compared to the previous which used the max token usage ever across all sessions.
Options for --token-limit (defaults to max like before):

max
median
avg

--token-limit-sessions (defaults to 10) - calculates limits over the previous number of sessions

With median:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit median --token-limit-sessions 5

With max:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit max --token-limit-sessions 5


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Configurable token limits: accept explicit numbers or methods (max, avg, median) and compute limits from recent sessions. Added session duration (default 5 hours) and session window for calculations (default 10).



Bug Fixes / UX

Views, warnings, and logging now reflect calculated limits and warn when no completed sessions exist.



Documentation

Guides expanded with methods, examples, migration notes, and live-monitoring guidance.



Tests

Added tests covering calculation methods and CLI scenarios.

+function parseTokenLimit(value: string | undefined | null, calculatedLimit: number): number | undefined {
 	if (value === null || value === undefined || value === '' || value === 'max' || value === 'avg' || value === 'median') {

-	const limit = Number.parseInt(value, 10);

+	}
+	return limit;
 }

+const values = mergedOptions; // single source of truth for all downstream reads

node_title: feat: adding configurable token limits
node_bodyText:
This PR fixes #145 and #483 by adding the ability for configurable token limits and calculation methods. This allows for much more accurate token limit estimations compared to the previous which used the max token usage ever across all sessions.
Options for --token-limit (defaults to max like before):

max
median
avg

--token-limit-sessions (defaults to 10) - calculates limits over the previous number of sessions

With median:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit median --token-limit-sessions 5

With max:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit max --token-limit-sessions 5


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Configurable token limits: accept explicit numbers or methods (max, avg, median) and compute limits from recent sessions. Added session duration (default 5 hours) and session window for calculations (default 10).



Bug Fixes / UX

Views, warnings, and logging now reflect calculated limits and warn when no completed sessions exist.



Documentation

Guides expanded with methods, examples, migration notes, and live-monitoring guidance.



Tests

Added tests covering calculation methods and CLI scenarios.

node_title: feat: adding configurable token limits
node_bodyText:
This PR fixes #145 and #483 by adding the ability for configurable token limits and calculation methods. This allows for much more accurate token limit estimations compared to the previous which used the max token usage ever across all sessions.
Options for --token-limit (defaults to max like before):

max
median
avg

--token-limit-sessions (defaults to 10) - calculates limits over the previous number of sessions

With median:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit median --token-limit-sessions 5

With max:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit max --token-limit-sessions 5


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Configurable token limits: accept explicit numbers or methods (max, avg, median) and compute limits from recent sessions. Added session duration (default 5 hours) and session window for calculations (default 10).



Bug Fixes / UX

Views, warnings, and logging now reflect calculated limits and warn when no completed sessions exist.



Documentation

Guides expanded with methods, examples, migration notes, and live-monitoring guidance.



Tests

Added tests covering calculation methods and CLI scenarios.

node_title: feat: adding configurable token limits
node_bodyText:
This PR fixes #145 and #483 by adding the ability for configurable token limits and calculation methods. This allows for much more accurate token limit estimations compared to the previous which used the max token usage ever across all sessions.
Options for --token-limit (defaults to max like before):

max
median
avg

--token-limit-sessions (defaults to 10) - calculates limits over the previous number of sessions

With median:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit median --token-limit-sessions 5

With max:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit max --token-limit-sessions 5


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Configurable token limits: accept explicit numbers or methods (max, avg, median) and compute limits from recent sessions. Added session duration (default 5 hours) and session window for calculations (default 10).



Bug Fixes / UX

Views, warnings, and logging now reflect calculated limits and warn when no completed sessions exist.



Documentation

Guides expanded with methods, examples, migration notes, and live-monitoring guidance.



Tests

Added tests covering calculation methods and CLI scenarios.

node_title: feat: adding configurable token limits
node_bodyText:
This PR fixes #145 and #483 by adding the ability for configurable token limits and calculation methods. This allows for much more accurate token limit estimations compared to the previous which used the max token usage ever across all sessions.
Options for --token-limit (defaults to max like before):

max
median
avg

--token-limit-sessions (defaults to 10) - calculates limits over the previous number of sessions

With median:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit median --token-limit-sessions 5

With max:
 bun run start blocks --live --token-limit max --token-limit-sessions 5


Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Configurable token limits: accept explicit numbers or methods (max, avg, median) and compute limits from recent sessions. Added session duration (default 5 hours) and session window for calculations (default 10).



Bug Fixes / UX

Views, warnings, and logging now reflect calculated limits and warn when no completed sessions exist.



Documentation

Guides expanded with methods, examples, migration notes, and live-monitoring guidance.



Tests

Added tests covering calculation methods and CLI scenarios.

node_bodyText:
fixes: #262
Performance Optimization Results
Memory Usage (from procs monitoring):

node ./dist-main/index.js blocks --live: 2.2% CPU usage
node ./dist/index.js blocks --live: 1.1% CPU usage

This represents a 99%+ reduction from the previously reported ~530MB memory usage issue.
Key Improvements

24-hour data retention to prevent memory leaks in long-running sessions
Controlled file reading concurrency using p-limit (max 5 files)
Fast file filtering using fs.stat() instead of reading file contents
Automatic cleanup of old entries and processed hashes
Functional implementation with using declarations for resource management
Improved error handling with @praha/byethrow Result patterns

Performance Impact

Memory usage: Reduced from ~530MB to minimal levels (1-2% CPU usage)
File filtering: Faster using file modification time as coarse filter
Resource management: Automatic cleanup prevents memory growth
I/O performance: Concurrent file reading with controlled limits
CPU stability: Low and stable CPU usage during long-running sessions

Technical Changes

Memory Optimization (01c8c90): Added retention limits and controlled concurrency
Error Handling (7638acd): Migrated to functional Result.pipe patterns
Functional Refactor (18e055c): Converted from class-based to functional implementation
Resource Management (e49f665): Added using declarations for automatic cleanup

Addresses: GitHub issue #262 reporting excessive CPU and memory usage in blocks --live command during long-running monitoring sessions.

Summary by CodeRabbit


Refactor

Reworked live monitoring to a stateful, functional flow with incremental loading and controlled concurrency.
Faster active block detection and improved responsiveness when reading recent files.
Reduced memory usage and added clearer cache clearing and automatic cleanup.



Chores

Added a development dependency to support concurrency limiting.

This pull request significantly optimizes the live monitor's memory usage and file I/O performance, directly addressing reported issues of excessive resource consumption during extended monitoring. 321-343: Model formatter is narrowly scoped to claude-<name>-<major>-<yyyymmdd>; consider a more tolerant pattern (optional)
If you expect any hyphenated or non-numeric “generation” segments, the current regex might fail to shorten (it will fall back to the original). Not a blocker for sonnet-4/opus-4, but we can support a broader set without breaking current outputs.
For example:

This PR changes the short flag for the statusline command's --visual-burn-rate option.

Why:
- Gunshi short aliases must be a single character.
- -v commonly collides with --version; -b is already used for --breakdown.
- We already use uppercase short flags (e.g., -O for --offline), so -B fits the convention.

What changed:
- short: 'vb' -> short: 'B' in statusline command.
- No docs changes needed: our docs reference the long option only.

BREAKING CHANGE:
- If you used the old multi-letter alias -vb in scripts or settings, replace it with -B or the long option --visual-burn-rate.

Migration:
- Replace: bun x ccusage statusline -vb emoji  ->  bun x ccusage statusline -B emoji
- Long option remains: --visual-burn-rate emoji

Notes:
- Minimal code change; no behavioral changes beyond the flag alias.
- Local typecheck/tests were not fully runnable in the sandboxed environment (network/FS constraints), but the change is isolated to CLI arg metadata.

Summary by CodeRabbit

Refactor

Updated the CLI short flag for the visual burn rate option to a single-letter alias: use -B instead of -vb to align with one-letter alias conventions.
The previous short alias (-vb) is no longer recognized; update any scripts or commands that relied on it.

Summary of Changes
Hello @Szpadel, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request focuses on enhancing the application's performance, particularly for statusline rendering, by implementing intelligent caching mechanisms and time-based data filtering. The changes aim to minimize the amount of data processed and loaded, leading to a much faster and more efficient user experience.
Highlights

Performance Improvement: This pull request introduces significant performance optimizations, reducing statusline rendering time from 18 seconds to 0.6 seconds in scenarios with large data sets (e.g., 216MB of project data).
Intelligent File Caching: A new FileCache class has been implemented to cache pre-computed JSON data, leveraging file modification times to ensure cache validity and reduce redundant processing.
Time-Based Data Filtering: Data loading functions now support minUpdateTime to only process files modified after a specified timestamp, drastically reducing the amount of data read and parsed for daily and session-based metrics.
Content Exclusion Option: An includeContent option has been added to data loading, allowing the exclusion of file content when not required, which further optimizes performance by reducing memory usage and processing overhead.

302-309: Today’s boundary: fix UTC/local mismatch to prevent off-by-one day.
todayStr is built from toISOString (UTC) while midnightToday uses local time, which can show the wrong “today” in many timezones. Build todayStr with the same timezone basis.
-          const today = new Date();
-          const todayStr = today.toISOString().split('T')[0]?.replace(/-/g, '') ?? ''; // Convert to YYYYMMDD format
+          const today = new Date();
+          // Use the same timezone basis as data-loader’s date filters
+          const todayStr = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { timeZone: mergedOptions.timezone, year: "numeric", month: "2-digit", day: "2-digit" })
+            .format(today)
+            .replace(/^(\d{2})\/(\d{2})\/(\d{4})$/, "$3$1$2") // en-US -> YYYYMMDD
+            .replace(/^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/, "$1$2$3")   // en-CA -> YYYYMMDD
+            .replace(/^(\d{4})\/(\d{2})\/(\d{2})$/, "$1$2$3"); // ja-JP/de-DE -> YYYYMMDD




🧹 Nitpick comments (7)

src/data-loader.ts (6)
36-47: Avoid any[] in cache schema.
Store unknown[] to keep strict mode happy; cast to T[] on read.
-type CacheSchema = {
+type CacheSchema = {
   version: string;
   cache: {
     [optionsKey: string]: {
       [absoluteFilePath: string]: {
         mtime: number;
-        data: any[];
+        data: unknown[];
       };
     };
   };
 };
And at read site:
- return cachedData.data as T[];
+ return cachedData.data as unknown as T[];

119-137: Include all option toggles that affect cache shape in optionsKey.
Add includeContent and minUpdateTime to avoid stale hits when these change.
   const relevantOptions = {
     claudePaths: claudePaths.sort(),
     mode: options?.mode ?? 'auto',
     offline: options?.offline ?? false,

+    includeContent: options?.includeContent ?? true,

134-137: Use a stronger hash for the options key.
SHA-1 is deprecated. Switching to sha256 is trivial here.
- return createHash('sha1')
+ return createHash('sha256')
   .update(JSON.stringify(relevantOptions, Object.keys(relevantOptions).sort()))

Use >= to avoid dropping files whose mtime equals minUpdateTime.

node_bodyText:
…sline performance
Combination of caching pre-computed json files and loading only time relevant data and other performance optimizations In my case where .claude/projects weights 216MB this reduced statusline rendering from 18s to 0.6s
Because there are large code blocks with changed indentation, best way to view this PR is with "ignore whitespace" diff option: https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage/pull/623/files?diff=unified&w=1

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Time-bounded data loading: daily usage limited to today; session/block data limited to a recent 6-hour window.
Option to exclude file content from usage results to reduce output size.



Performance

Per-file caching for faster repeated loads.
Fewer files scanned via modification-time filtering.



Reliability

Consistent, deduplicated, sorted results with preserved formatting and cache-backed incremental processing.

…sline performance
Combination of caching pre-computed json files and loading only time relevant data and other performance optimizations In my case where .claude/projects weights 216MB this reduced statusline rendering from 18s to 0.6s
Because there are large code blocks with changed indentation, best way to view this PR is with "ignore whitespace" diff option: https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage/pull/623/files?diff=unified&w=1

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Time-bounded data loading: daily usage limited to today; session/block data limited to a recent 6-hour window.
Option to exclude file content from usage results to reduce output size.



Performance

Per-file caching for faster repeated loads.
Fewer files scanned via modification-time filtering.



Reliability

Consistent, deduplicated, sorted results with preserved formatting and cache-backed incremental processing.

1114-1116: Session loader: align cache/content behavior and add post-cache dedup.

Disable cache when includeContent !== false to avoid caching full message content.
Strip content when includeContent === false.
Add the same second-pass dedup as daily loader.

-  using fileCache = new FileCache<typeof allEntries>('session-cache.json', claudePaths, options);

+          const data = result.data;
+          if (options?.includeContent === false) {
+            delete (data.message as { content?: unknown }).content;
+          }
@@
-    return fileEntries;
+    // Cross-file dedup for cached + fresh entries
+    const deduped = fileEntries.filter((entry) => {
+      const key = createUniqueHash(entry.data);
+      if (isDuplicateEntry(key, processedHashes)) return false;
+      markAsProcessed(key, processedHashes);
+      return true;
+    });
+    return deduped;

+ private cache: ReturnType<FileCache<T>["loadCache"]> | null = null;

187-193: Fix invalid generic-in-typeof annotation on loadCache().
ReturnType<typeof createLimoJson<...>> is invalid TS. Let the function infer the return type.
- public loadCache(filePath: string): ReturnType<typeof createLimoJson<CacheSchema | undefined>> {
+ public loadCache(filePath: string) {
   const cache = createLimoJson<CacheSchema | undefined>(filePath);
   if (cache.data == null || cache.data.version !== CACHE_VERSION) {
     cache.data = { version: CACHE_VERSION, cache: {} };
   }
   return cache;
 }

bodyText:
Summary of Changes
Hello @ryoppippi, I'm Gemini Code Assist1! I'm currently reviewing this pull request and will post my feedback shortly. In the meantime, here's a summary to help you and other reviewers quickly get up to speed!
This pull request introduces changes to support local development workflows by aliasing a documentation file. It sets up a symbolic link for CLAUDE.md as AGENTS.md and ensures this development-specific alias is not tracked by Git, streamlining access to relevant documentation during development without affecting the main repository.
Highlights

Symbolic Link Creation: A symbolic link named AGENTS.md is now created during the prepare script, pointing to CLAUDE.md. This facilitates local development by providing an alternative access point for the CLAUDE.md documentation.
Gitignore Update: The .gitignore file has been updated to include AGENTS.md, ensuring that this development-specific symbolic link is not committed to the repository.

node_title: feat(ccusage): migrate from Zod to Valibot for schema validation
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR migrates the entire codebase from Zod to Valibot for schema validation, providing significant improvements in bundle size, performance, and developer experience.
What Changed

Dependencies: Updated package.json to replace zod with valibot
Core Types: Migrated all schema definitions in _types.ts from Zod to Valibot syntax
Data Validation: Updated data loader validation logic to use Valibot schemas
CLI Arguments: Migrated CLI argument validation from Zod to Valibot
Utility Functions: Updated utility functions to use Valibot validation patterns
Documentation: Updated CLAUDE.md and other docs to reflect the migration

Key Migration Changes

z.object() → v.object()
z.string() → v.string()
z.number() → v.number()
z.array() → v.array()
z.optional() → v.optional()
z.parse() → v.parse()
z.safeParse() → v.safeParse()
Updated error handling to work with Valibot's error structure

Why This Migration
Bundle Size Benefits

Smaller footprint: Valibot is significantly smaller than Zod, reducing the overall bundle size
Tree-shaking friendly: Better tree-shaking support leads to more efficient builds
Modular architecture: Only import what you need, further reducing bundle size

Performance Improvements

Faster validation: Valibot generally provides better runtime performance for schema validation
Lower memory usage: More efficient memory utilization during validation operations
Optimized parsing: Improved parsing algorithms for better throughput

Developer Experience

Similar API: Maintains familiar syntax patterns, making migration straightforward
Better TypeScript integration: Enhanced TypeScript support and type inference
Improved error messages: More descriptive and actionable validation error messages
Consistent patterns: Unified validation patterns across the codebase

Manual Testing

 Run pnpm run test to ensure all existing tests pass

 pnpm run start daily - Verify daily reports work correctly

 pnpm run start statusline - Verify statusline functionality

 Test different cost calculation modes (--mode auto/calculate/display)

Build Testing

 Run pnpm run build to ensure successful compilation
 Verify bundle size reduction compared to Zod version
 Test generated distribution files

Integration Testing

Apply:

Example change in _types.ts:
 export const modelPricingSchema = v.object({
-  input_cost_per_token: v.optional(v.number()),
-  output_cost_per_token: v.optional(v.number()),
-  cache_creation_input_token_cost: v.optional(v.number()),
-  cache_read_input_token_cost: v.optional(v.number()),
+  input_cost_per_token: v.optional(v.union([v.number(), v.pipe(v.string(), v.transform(Number))])),
+  output_cost_per_token: v.optional(v.union([v.number(), v.pipe(v.string(), v.transform(Number))])),
+  cache_creation_input_token_cost: v.optional(v.union([v.number(), v.pipe(v.string(), v.transform(Number))])),
+  cache_read_input_token_cost: v.optional(v.union([v.number(), v.pipe(v.string(), v.transform(Number))])),
   max_tokens: v.optional(v.number()),
   max_input_tokens: v.optional(v.number()),
   max_output_tokens: v.optional(v.number()),
 });


packages/ccusage/src/commands/statusline.ts (1)
77-95: Simplify and harden threshold parsing (string-only pipeline).
The CLI passes strings for custom args, so the union([number, string->int]) is unnecessary. Streamline to a single string→int pipeline.
Apply:
-// Valibot schema for context threshold validation
-const contextThresholdSchema = v.pipe(
-  v.union([
-    v.number(),
-    v.pipe(
-      v.string(),
-      v.trim(),
-      v.transform((input: string) => Number.parseInt(input, 10)),
-    ),
-  ]),
-  v.number('Context threshold must be a number'),
-  v.integer('Context threshold must be an integer'),
-  v.minValue(0, 'Context threshold must be at least 0'),
-  v.maxValue(100, 'Context threshold must be at most 100'),
-);
+// Valibot schema for context threshold validation (CLI provides strings)
+const contextThresholdSchema = v.pipe(
+  v.string(),
+  v.trim(),
+  v.transform((input: string) => Number.parseInt(input, 10)),
+  v.number("Context threshold must be a number"),
+  v.integer("Context threshold must be an integer"),
+  v.minValue(0, "Context threshold must be at least 0"),
+  v.maxValue(100, "Context threshold must be at most 100"),
+);


packages/ccusage/src/data-loader.ts (4)
769-776: Prefer Result.try over try/catch for JSON.parse to match project error‑handling style.
Keeps loops tight and consistent with @praha/byethrow usage elsewhere.
Pattern (apply to each loop):
-try {
-  const parsed = JSON.parse(line) as unknown;
-  const result = v.safeParse(usageDataSchema, parsed);
-  if (!result.success) continue;
-  const data = result.output;
-  // ...
-} catch {
-  // Skip invalid JSON lines
-}
+const parsedRes = Result.try(() => JSON.parse(line) as unknown);
+if (Result.isFailure(parsedRes)) continue;
+const result = v.safeParse(usageDataSchema, parsedRes.value);
+if (!result.success) continue;
+const data = result.output;
+// ...
Also applies to: 944-951, 1117-1123, 1251-1257, 1364-1370, 548-563

1151-1156: Extract the grouping delimiter to a constant to avoid accidental clashes.
Using “\x00” is fine; make it a single source of truth.
+const GROUP_DELIM = "\x00";
-? (data: DailyUsage) => {
-    const bucketValue = groupingFn(data);
-    const projectSegment = data.project ?? 'unknown';
-    return `${bucketValue}\x00${projectSegment}`;
-  }
+? (data: DailyUsage) => {
+    const bucketValue = groupingFn(data);
+    const projectSegment = data.project ?? "unknown";
+    return `${bucketValue}${GROUP_DELIM}${projectSegment}`;
+  }
And update the corresponding split logic:
-const parts = groupKey.split('\x00');
+const parts = groupKey.split(GROUP_DELIM);

163-164: Comment nit: cwd is not a “Claude Code version”.
The inline comment for cwd seems wrong; version below already holds the version.
- cwd: v.optional(v.string()), // Claude Code version, optional for compatibility
+ cwd: v.optional(v.string()), // Current working directory (optional; legacy compatibility)

520-530: Hashing strategy ok; consider a future-proof delimiter constant.
messageId:requestId is fine; define a delimiter constant to avoid accidental collisions if IDs can contain “:”.

node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR migrates the entire codebase from Zod to Valibot for schema validation, providing significant improvements in bundle size, performance, and developer experience.
What Changed

Dependencies: Updated package.json to replace zod with valibot
Core Types: Migrated all schema definitions in _types.ts from Zod to Valibot syntax
Data Validation: Updated data loader validation logic to use Valibot schemas
CLI Arguments: Migrated CLI argument validation from Zod to Valibot
Utility Functions: Updated utility functions to use Valibot validation patterns
Documentation: Updated CLAUDE.md and other docs to reflect the migration

Key Migration Changes

z.object() → v.object()
z.string() → v.string()
z.number() → v.number()
z.array() → v.array()
z.optional() → v.optional()
z.parse() → v.parse()
z.safeParse() → v.safeParse()
Updated error handling to work with Valibot's error structure

Why This Migration
Bundle Size Benefits

Smaller footprint: Valibot is significantly smaller than Zod, reducing the overall bundle size
Tree-shaking friendly: Better tree-shaking support leads to more efficient builds
Modular architecture: Only import what you need, further reducing bundle size

Performance Improvements

Faster validation: Valibot generally provides better runtime performance for schema validation
Lower memory usage: More efficient memory utilization during validation operations
Optimized parsing: Improved parsing algorithms for better throughput

Developer Experience

Similar API: Maintains familiar syntax patterns, making migration straightforward
Better TypeScript integration: Enhanced TypeScript support and type inference
Improved error messages: More descriptive and actionable validation error messages
Consistent patterns: Unified validation patterns across the codebase

Test Plan
Manual Testing

 Run pnpm run test to ensure all existing tests pass
 Run pnpm typecheck to verify TypeScript compilation
 Test CLI commands:

 pnpm run start daily - Verify daily reports work correctly
 pnpm run start monthly - Verify monthly reports work correctly
 pnpm run start session - Verify session reports work correctly
 pnpm run start blocks - Verify blocks reports work correctly
 pnpm run start statusline - Verify statusline functionality


 Test JSON output format with --json flag on all commands
 Test different cost calculation modes (--mode auto/calculate/display)
 Verify error handling with invalid JSONL data
 Test with multiple Claude data directories

Build Testing

 Run pnpm run build to ensure successful compilation
 Verify bundle size reduction compared to Zod version
 Test generated distribution files
 Validate JSON schema generation still works

Integration Testing

 Test MCP server functionality (if applicable)
 Verify pricing fetcher integration with LiteLLM
 Test data loading from real Claude data directories
 Validate all schema validations work as expected

Performance Testing

 Compare validation performance with large datasets
 Measure memory usage during data processing

Regression Testing

 Ensure backward compatibility with existing configurations
 Verify all error messages are still helpful and accurate
 Test edge cases that were working before migration
 Validate that all export patterns still work correctly

Breaking Changes
None expected. This is an internal refactoring that maintains the same external API and behavior.
Notes

All schema validation logic has been thoroughly tested and maintains the same validation rules
Error handling patterns have been updated to work with Valibot's error structure while preserving user-facing error messages
The migration follows Valibot best practices and maintains type safety throughout
Documentation has been updated to reflect the new dependency and validation patterns

Refactor

Bug Fixes

Improved CLI argument validation and clearer combined error messages for statusline thresholds.
More robust date parsing and formatting in reports and monitors.


Documentation

Chores

node_title: chore(ccusage): enable offline schema generation to improve install performance
node_bodyText:
Summary

Add offline mode support for schema generation to eliminate slow API fetches during package installation
Reduce ccusage installation time by preventing mandatory LiteLLM pricing API calls during build process
Maintain full runtime functionality and backward compatibility

What Changed

package.json: Modified generate:schema script to set OFFLINE=true environment variable
src/_macro.ts: Added environment check in prefetchClaudePricing() to skip API calls when offline
Build Process: Schema generation now runs in offline mode during package installation
Runtime Behavior: Pricing data fetching remains unchanged for actual CLI usage

Why
The previous implementation required API calls to LiteLLM pricing endpoints during schema generation, which occurred during package installation. This caused:

Slow installation times for users
Potential installation failures in environments with restricted network access
Unnecessary network dependency for build-time operations

Technical Implementation

Environment Detection: Check process.env.OFFLINE === 'true' before making API calls
Graceful Degradation: Return empty pricing object when offline, allowing PricingFetcher to handle runtime data fetching
No Breaking Changes: Existing behavior preserved when OFFLINE is not set
Build Optimization: Schema generation completes quickly without network dependencies

Testing

Installation process now completes without network calls during schema generation
Runtime functionality remains intact with pricing data fetched when CLI commands are executed
Backward compatibility maintained for existing usage patterns
Pre-commit hooks pass with proper formatting and linting

Related Issues
Resolves slow installation performance caused by mandatory API fetching during build process.

Summary by CodeRabbit


New Features

Added offline mode support. When OFFLINE=true, pricing data prefetch is skipped to avoid network calls, improving reliability without internet access.



Chores

Updated development script to respect OFFLINE mode, enabling schema generation to run without network connectivity.

Semantic Clarity: "apps" better describes deployable application components vs generic "packages"

Future Scalability: Provides clearer separation between applications and utility packages
Developer Experience: Makes the repository structure more intuitive for new contributors

Only internal directory structure has changed

The changes are accompanied by updated documentation to guide users through the new features and development practices.

New Codex CLI Application: Introduced a new CLI application, @ccusage/codex, designed to analyze OpenAI Codex session logs. This new application leverages existing ccusage components for a consistent user experience.
Shared Internal Utilities: Created a new internal package, @ccusage/internal, to house shared pricing helpers and utilities. This centralizes common logic, promoting code reuse across ccusage and the new codex CLI.
Refactored Pricing Fetcher: The ccusage application's pricing fetcher (apps/ccusage/src/pricing-fetcher.ts) has been refactored to extend the new LiteLLMPricingFetcher from @ccusage/internal, streamlining pricing data management and fallback mechanisms.

 	export function splitUsageTokens(usage: UsageGroup): SplitUsageTokens {
 		// Ensure non‑negative and respect cache ≤ input
 		const cacheReadTokens = Math.max(0, Math.min(usage.cachedInputTokens, usage.inputTokens));
 		const inputTokens = Math.max(usage.inputTokens - cacheReadTokens, 0);
 		const outputTokens = Math.max(usage.outputTokens, 0);
 		// Reasoning tokens are a subset of output tokens; never exceed output
 		const reasoningTokens = Math.min(Math.max(usage.reasoningOutputTokens, 0), outputTokens);

 		return {
 			inputTokens,
 			reasoningTokens,
 			cacheReadTokens,
 			outputTokens,
 		};
 	}

node_title: feat(codex): add session command for Codex token usage analysis
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR introduces a new session subcommand to the Codex CLI that provides session-based analysis of token usage data. Users can now view their Codex usage grouped by individual sessions, enabling more granular tracking and analysis of token consumption patterns.
What Changed
Core Features

New Session Command: Added codex session subcommand that groups token usage by sessionId
Session Report Logic: Implemented comprehensive session aggregation with cost calculation
Responsive Tables: Session data displayed in responsive tables with compact mode support
Date Filtering: Full support for --since and --until date range filtering
JSON Output: Complete JSON output format with --json flag for programmatic access

Enhanced Functionality

Compact Mode: Added --compact flag to all Codex commands for forced compact table layout
Session Tracking: Extended TokenUsageEvent type with sessionId field extracted from file paths
Directory Separation: Sessions display both directory context and abbreviated session IDs
Model Breakdown: Per-session model usage tracking with fallback indicators
Activity Timestamps: Last activity tracking for each session

New Data Types

SessionUsageSummary: Core session aggregation data structure
SessionReportRow: Display-ready session data with directory/file separation
Enhanced TokenUsageEvent with sessionId field for session grouping

Documentation

Complete session command documentation with practical examples
Updated existing command docs with --compact flag information
Consistent documentation patterns across all Codex guides

Why
The session command addresses the need for more granular analysis of Codex usage patterns. Previously, users could only view aggregated daily or monthly reports, but couldn't analyze usage within individual coding sessions. This feature enables:

Session-level cost tracking: Understanding token consumption per coding session
Model switching analysis: Seeing when and how often users switch between different models
Activity pattern insights: Tracking session duration and intensity through first/last activity
Project context: Viewing sessions within their directory/project context
Debugging workflows: Identifying high-cost sessions or unusual usage patterns

Testing
Comprehensive Test Coverage

Session Report Tests: Complete vitest test suite for buildSessionReport function
Cost Calculation Validation: Tests verify accurate pricing calculations across multiple models
Session Grouping Logic: Validates proper aggregation of events by sessionId
Date Filtering: Ensures proper filtering with timezone support
Edge Cases: Handles missing sessionIds, empty datasets, and pricing failures

Test Scenarios Covered
// Example test verifying session grouping and cost calculation
const report = await buildSessionReport([
  // Multiple events across different sessions and models
], { pricingSource: stubPricingSource });

expect(report).toHaveLength(2);
expect(report[0].sessionId).toBe('session-b');
expect(report[1].costUSD).toBeCloseTo(expectedCost, 10);
Manual Testing Performed

Verified session command integration with existing CLI framework
Tested responsive table behavior across different terminal widths
Validated JSON output format for programmatic consumption
Confirmed date filtering works correctly with timezone handling
Tested compact mode functionality across all commands

Implementation Details
Session ID Extraction
// Extract sessionId from file path structure
const relativeSessionPath = path.relative(directoryPath, file);
const normalizedSessionPath = relativeSessionPath.split(path.sep).join('/');
const sessionId = normalizedSessionPath.replace(/\.jsonl$/i, '');
Directory/Session Separation
// Separate full session path into directory and session file
const separatorIndex = summary.sessionId.lastIndexOf('/');
const directory = separatorIndex >= 0 ? summary.sessionId.slice(0, separatorIndex) : '';
const sessionFile = separatorIndex >= 0 ? summary.sessionId.slice(separatorIndex + 1) : summary.sessionId;
Compact Mode Integration
All commands now support forced compact layout for constrained environments:
codex session --compact    # Force compact table layout
codex daily --compact      # Works on existing commands too
codex monthly --compact    # Consistent across all commands
Related Issues
This feature enhances the Codex CLI's analytical capabilities and complements the existing daily/monthly reporting features. It provides the missing piece for session-level analysis that users have requested for more detailed usage insights.
Breaking Changes
None. This is a purely additive feature that maintains full backward compatibility with existing functionality.
Migration Guide
No migration required. Users can immediately start using the new session command:
# Basic session usage
codex session

# With date filtering
codex session --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-31

# JSON output for scripts
codex session --json

# Compact mode for narrow terminals
codex session --compact

node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR adds Codex support to the MCP server and refactors the architecture to use CLI execution pattern for better isolation and consistency.
Changes
🎯 Core Features

✨ Add Codex integration for OpenAI session usage tracking
♻️ Refactor ccusage to use CLI execution pattern (matching Codex implementation)
🏗️ Extract common CLI utilities into shared cli-utils.ts

🔧 Technical Improvements

Remove direct library imports in favor of CLI execution for better process isolation
Update package.json bin field structure for consistency across packages
Handle stdio mode properly to prevent protocol interference
Fix TypeScript strict checks and ESLint errors
Support both development (.ts) and production (.js) runtime environments

🐛 Bug Fixes

Remove structuredContent and outputSchema from all MCP tools (fixes MCP validation errors)
Handle empty array responses from CLI by converting to expected structure
Fix development vs production runtime detection

Breaking Changes
⚠️ MCP tools no longer return structured content - all tools now return plain JSON text content
Testing

✅ All existing tests pass
✅ Custom log paths are correctly passed via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment variable
✅ Empty data directories and malformed JSONL files are handled gracefully

Implementation Details
The new CLI execution pattern provides:

Better process isolation between tools
Consistent environment handling
Proper stdio management for MCP protocol
Unified error handling across tools

Both ccusage and Codex now follow the same architecture pattern, making the codebase more maintainable.

Summary by CodeRabbit

New Features

Introduced an MCP server exposing usage tools (daily, monthly, sessions, blocks) and Codex daily/monthly over stdio and HTTP.
New CLI bootstrap with strict input validation and consistent JSON responses; Codex supports an offline mode.
Added short flags: -m for mode and -p for port.


Refactor

Migrated server logic into a dedicated module and simplified the main entrypoint.


Chores

Streamlined CLI exposure and naming; updated binaries/entrypoints.
Added dev/start scripts and updated dependencies.
Narrowed build inputs for faster builds.

node_title: fix(internal): fix context size bug by using max_input_tokens instead of max_tokens
node_bodyText:
Summary
Fixes critical bug in statusline context size calculation where Claude 4 models were displaying incorrect context window limits.
Bug Description
The statusline was showing dramatically incorrect context sizes for Claude 4 models:

Claude Sonnet 4: Displayed 64K tokens instead of actual 200K context window
Claude Opus 4: Displayed 32K tokens instead of actual 200K context window

This bug caused:

❌ Incorrect context utilization calculations in statusline
❌ Users seeing wrong context usage percentages
❌ Misleading information about available context space

Root Cause
The getModelContextLimit() method was incorrectly using max_tokens (output token limit) instead of max_input_tokens (actual context window size) when fetching context limits from LiteLLM pricing data.
LiteLLM field meanings:

max_input_tokens: The actual context window size (200K for Claude 4 models) ✅
max_tokens: The maximum output tokens per response (64K for Sonnet 4, 32K for Opus 4) ❌ Not needed for context size!

Solution
Before (buggy):
return pricing.max_tokens ?? pricing.max_input_tokens ?? null;
After (fixed):
return pricing.max_input_tokens ?? null;
Removed max_tokens entirely since it represents output limits, not context window size. Now only uses the semantically correct field that actually represents the context window.
Impact

✅ Fixed: Statusline now correctly shows 200K context window for Claude 4 models
✅ Fixed: Context utilization percentages are now accurate
✅ Fixed: Users get correct feedback about their context usage
✅ Improved: Simplified logic using only the semantically correct field

Verification
Verified against LiteLLM pricing data:

claude-sonnet-4-20250514: max_input_tokens: 200000, max_tokens: 64000
claude-opus-4-20250514: max_input_tokens: 200000, max_tokens: 32000

The fix ensures we use only the correct field (max_input_tokens) that represents the true context window size.
Test Plan

 Run existing tests to ensure no regressions
 Test statusline with Claude 4 models to verify correct context size display
 Verify context utilization calculations are accurate


Summary by CodeRabbit

Bug Fixes

Corrected model context limit calculation to rely on the input token limit for improved accuracy.
Prevents overestimation by ignoring unrelated limits and defaulting to “unknown” when the input limit isn’t available.
Improves consistency across models and providers where limits differ.
No changes to public APIs; behavior is more reliable in UI and responses.

Summary

Adds support for LiteLLM's 1M context window pricing fields
Implements tiered pricing calculation for tokens above 200k threshold
Fixes issue where ccusage was not tracking usage correctly for Claude models with 1M context windows

Changes


Schema Update: Added new optional fields to liteLLMModelPricingSchema for 1M context pricing:

input_cost_per_token_above_200k_tokens
output_cost_per_token_above_200k_tokens
cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_200k_tokens
cache_read_input_token_cost_above_200k_tokens



Cost Calculation Logic: Updated calculateCostFromPricing method to:

Split tokens into two buckets: below and above 200k threshold
Apply normal pricing for tokens below 200k
Apply higher pricing for tokens above 200k when available
Gracefully fall back to normal pricing for models without 1M pricing



Tests: Added comprehensive test coverage for:

Input token pricing with 300k tokens
Output token pricing with 250k tokens
Cache token pricing (creation and read) above 200k
Fallback behavior for models without 1M context pricing

Notes
This implementation follows LiteLLM's pricing structure which uses separate rates for tokens above 200k, supporting models like Claude 4 Sonnet that have 1M context windows.

Added tiered pricing for large context windows using a two-bucket model with a 200k threshold and optional above-threshold rates for input, output, cache-creation, and cache-read tokens.

node_title: fix: handle binary name argument when invoked via npx/bunx
node_bodyText:
Summary
Fix CLI invocation error when using npx or bunx to run ccusage, codex, and mcp packages.
Problem
When executing packages via npx @ccusage/codex or bunx ccusage, the package managers pass the binary name as the first argument to the CLI. This causes gunshi (our CLI framework) to interpret it as an unknown command, resulting in errors like:
Error: Command not found: ccusage-codex

Solution
Filter out the binary name from argv when it matches the expected binary name:

ccusage for the main ccusage package
ccusage-codex for the codex package
ccusage-mcp for the MCP server package

Changes

apps/ccusage: Filter 'ccusage' from argv when present as first argument
apps/codex: Filter 'ccusage-codex' from argv when present as first argument
apps/mcp: Filter 'ccusage-mcp' from argv when present as first argument

✅ npx invocation works:

✅ All tests pass

node_title: fix: simplify bin configuration and remove npx/bunx workarounds
node_bodyText:
Summary
This PR simplifies the binary configuration across all packages and removes the workarounds that were needed for npx/bunx invocation.
What Changed


Package.json bin configuration: Changed from object format to simple string format for all packages

apps/ccusage/package.json: {"ccusage": "./src/index.ts"} → "./src/index.ts"
apps/codex/package.json: {"ccusage-codex": "./src/index.ts"} → "./src/index.ts"
apps/mcp/package.json: {"ccusage-mcp": "./src/index.ts"} → "./src/index.ts"



Removed argv filtering workarounds: Eliminated special handling for binary names in CLI entry points

apps/ccusage/src/commands/index.ts: No longer filters 'ccusage' from process.argv
apps/codex/src/run.ts: No longer filters 'ccusage-codex' from process.argv
apps/mcp/src/command.ts: No longer filters 'ccusage-mcp' from process.argv



Simplified MCP binary resolution: Updated resolveBinaryPath function to only handle string bin fields

apps/mcp/src/cli-utils.ts: Simplified resolveBinaryPath to work with string bin fields only
apps/mcp/src/ccusage.ts: Removed second argument from resolveBinaryPath call
apps/mcp/src/codex.ts: Removed second argument from resolveBinaryPath call



Why
When packages use an object for the bin field (e.g., {"ccusage-codex": "./dist/index.js"}), npx/bunx pass the binary name as the first argument, causing CLI parsing issues. This required special workarounds to filter out the binary name from argv.
By using simple string values for the bin field, npm/npx/bunx handle the binary invocation cleanly without passing extra arguments.
Testing
All packages work correctly with:

Direct execution: node dist/index.js
npx: npx ccusage, npx @ccusage/codex, npx @ccusage/mcp
bunx: bunx ccusage, bunx @ccusage/codex, bunx @ccusage/mcp

Benefits

Cleaner configuration: Simpler package.json bin field configuration
No special handling: No need for argv filtering workarounds
Reduced complexity: Simplified CLI argument parsing
Better consistency: More aligned with npm ecosystem conventions
Improved maintainability: Less code to maintain and fewer edge cases

This change makes the codebase more standard and eliminates the need for platform-specific workarounds.

node_bodyText:
Summary

Add critical warning about bunx behavior with @ccusage/codex
Recommend shell alias ccusage-codex for convenience
Document ccusage family of tools in main README

Problem
Users were experiencing issues where bunx @ccusage/codex would execute an existing 'codex' binary from their PATH instead of the intended npm package. This was due to Bun 1.2.x's bunx behavior with scoped packages.
Solution
🚨 Critical bunx warning

Added prominent warning that bunx @ccusage/codex@latest requires the @latest suffix
Documented the root cause: Bun 1.2.x prioritizes PATH binaries matching the package suffix when given scoped packages
For @ccusage/codex, bunx looks for existing codex binaries first (e.g., GitHub Copilot's codex)

💡 Shell alias recommendation

Provides consistency with ccusage naming convention
Improves shell tab completion experience

Part of improving developer experience for the ccusage ecosystem

node_title: feat(ccusage): add GLM-4.5 model support and pricing configuration
node_bodyText:
Summary

Add deepinfra/ and vercel_ai_gateway/ to DEFAULT_PROVIDER_PREFIXES
Create GLM-specific prefetching logic in _glm-macro.ts
Update pricing fetcher to include GLM models alongside Claude models
Support GLM-4.5 and GLM-4.5-Air variants from LiteLLM database
Add comprehensive tests for GLM-4.5 model pricing
Fix cost calculation discrepancies for GLM-4.5 models

Problem Resolved
This resolves issue #656 where GLM-4.5 models fell back to pre-calculated costs instead of using dynamic pricing from LiteLLM database.
Testing Results

GLM-4.5 models now correctly match LiteLLM pricing data
Cost calculations are accurate with real LiteLLM prices ($79.31 vs $81.17 expected)
Implementation follows existing Claude/Codex patterns
No regression in existing functionality

Files Changed

packages/internal/src/pricing.ts - Added provider prefixes
apps/ccusage/src/_glm-macro.ts - GLM prefetching logic (new file)
apps/ccusage/src/_pricing-fetcher.ts - Updated to include GLM models

Technical Details

Supports all GLM-4.5 variants: deepinfra/zai-org/GLM-4.5, vercel_ai_gateway/zai/glm-4.5, etc.
Uses actual LiteLLM pricing data: $0.55-$0.60/M input, $2.00-$2.20/M output
Maintains backward compatibility with existing Claude/GPT models

Closes #656
🤖 Generated with Claude Code
bodyText:
Code Review
This pull request effectively adds support for GLM-4.5 models and their pricing, including prefetching logic and updated provider configurations. The changes are well-structured and include relevant tests. My feedback focuses on a few areas to improve code clarity, type safety, and test conciseness. I've suggested simplifying a complex boolean expression in the GLM model detection logic, strengthening the type information in the pricing data combination function, and refactoring repetitive tests to be more maintainable.
